services.title: Deploy Capital
services.desc: Catalytic grants and concessional finance tailored to locally-led restoration champions across Africa's diverse landscapes.
body: VIA Foundation and its partners deploy grants, debt, and equity directly to the organisations doing restoration work on the ground — cooperatives, social enterprises, and community associations.

Funding is structured around each organization’s growth stage, from early seed grants that de-risk a first pilot to larger multi-year commitments that help proven models scale. Every disbursement is paired with clear, achievable milestones co-designed with the partner, so capital keeps pace with real capacity rather than forcing premature scale.

services.title: Build Capacity
services.desc: Hands-on capacity building, knowledge transfer and implementation support to strengthen restoration organizations at scale.
body: Money alone doesn't restore land — organisations need financial management systems, monitoring capability, and technical know-how to deploy it well. VIA Foundation's technical assistance team works side-by-side with local organizations to build exactly that.

Support spans from nursery management and agroforestry techniques to financial reporting, governance structures, and safeguarding practices, delivered through peer exchanges and online courses. The goal is durable institutional strength: organisations that can attract and manage more finance.

services.title: Manage Portfolios & Performance
services.desc: Rigorous impact measurement, satellite monitoring and third-party verification ensuring accountability and transparency.
body: Every hectare VIA Foundation finances is tracked thoroughly by its experienced project managers and field coordinators. Hands-on technical support helps local organizations solve challenges in real time.

Reports every six months and structured field visits bring in constant data on portfolio performance. This system flags underperforming sites early, allowing VIA Foundation and its partners to adapt before problems compound.

services.title: Blended Finance
services.desc: Innovative financial instruments that mobilize private capital alongside public funding for maximum restoration leverage.
body: VIA Foundation structures blended finance vehicles that combine catalytic public and philanthropic capital with private investment, reducing risk for commercial funders entering restoration for the first time.
Instruments range from first-loss guarantees and outcome-based payments to co-investment facilities designed alongside development banks and impact investors.
By absorbing early-stage risk, VIA Foundation helps unlock capital at a scale that grants alone could never reach.

priorityLandscapes.title: Lake Kivu & Rusizi Basin
body: VIA Foundation operates in three key landscapes, where restoration strengthens the ecological integrity of degraded landscapes while delivering social and economic benefits to local communities.

In the Lake Kivu & Rusizi Basin spanning Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Rwanda, planting trees helps to reduce operating costs for hydropower companies and protect habitat for endangered biodiversity.

priorityLandscapes.title: Kenya’s Greater Rift Valley
body: In Kenya’s Greater Rift Valley, restoration reduces flood risks and protects water supplies for flower exporters, geothermal operators, and smallholder farms.

priorityLandscapes.title: Ghana Cocoa Belt
body: In the Ghana Cocoa Belt, the shift to shade-grown cocoa helps cocoa companies comply with new deforestation regulations and increases farms’ resilience to climate change.

implementationPartnerships.title: TerraFund
body: Founded by the World Resources Institute (WRI), One Tree Planted, and Realize Impact in 2021, TerraFund is a financing partnership that has deployed grants, loans, and equity investments ranging from $50,000 to $500,000 to community-based non-profits and enterprises restoring land.

Since 2025, VIA Foundation has helped manage 141 TerraFund projects, with staff co-creating projects alongside community-based organizations and enterprises. This partnership has helped VIA Foundation build its track record of targeting investments to maximize impact per dollar, deploying flexible funding, and providing monitoring and verification support for a real-time view of restoration progress.

implementationPartnerships.title: Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Bond
body: Restoration-linked bonds offer a new way to close the restoration finance gap. As a form of outcome-based finance, these instruments direct bond proceeds straight to restoration projects. Instead of receiving coupon payments, investors are repaid at maturity through outcome payments tied to achieving pre-agreed restoration goals. As a result, outcome payers only pay for verified, measurable restoration outcomes.

The Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Bond, issued by the World Bank and the Government of Rwanda, is designed to channel funding to restore 3,000 hectares of chimpanzee habitat in and around Gishwati-Mukura and Nyungwe National Parks in Rwanda’s Western Province. VIA Foundation serves as an outcome payer, further mobilizing commitments from the Global Environmental Facility and Climate Investment Funds.

implementationPartnerships.title: Revolving Capital Facility
body: Through this facility, VIA Foundation creates a virtuous circle in which capital is repaid through verified outcomes and reinvested in new restoration projects. The RCF works in five steps: raising upfront capital, securing outcome commitments, funding local delivery, verifying and repaying, and reinvesting for greater impact.
VIA Foundation is actively mobilizing commitments from upfront financiers, as well as outcome payers, to kickstart the facility in each of the three priority landscapes.

implementationPartnerships.title: W+ Credits for Gender & Social Equity
body: VIA Foundation is partnering with WOCAN to certify the gender and social equity outcomes of its portfolio and issue credits to outcome payers. Women are central to restoration, yet often do not receive financial benefits or recognition for their work.

VIA Foundation serves as a project developer, identifying leading local organizations from its portfolio and directing grant funding to implement women’s empowerment initiatives. Currently, VIA Foundation is piloting this approach with two projects in Kenya, before expanding to additional partners.

projects.name: The Network for Natural Gums and Resins in Africa (NGARA)
projects.excerpt:
Africa supplies much of the world’s natural gum, aloe, and resins. But these high-quality crops are grown in drylands, which suffer from inconsistent rains and pervasive poverty. Non-profit organization NGARA helps African countries that produce natural gum and resins to find sustainable ways of growing, harvesting and marketing them to improve community livelihoods and conserve precious water.

This grant will help the organization increase the number of gum-producing Acacia senegal trees and indigenous aloe plants in Baringo, Elgeyo Marakwet, and West Pokot Counties in Kenya. This work will connect farmers across the region to new opportunities for income in these growing value chains.

projects.name: Nature Kenya - the East Africa Natural History Society (EANHS)
projects.excerpt:
Nature Kenya is Africa's oldest environmental society. Established in 1909, the organization aims is to promote the study and conservation of nature in Eastern Africa. Nature Kenya’s biodiversity conservation focuses on globally recognized Important Bird Areas (IBAs) and Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs). The organization has restored 10,000 hectares of land in the last three years and grown 10,000,000 trees.

Nature Kenya will use this grant to restore the Cherangani Hills Forest through direct tree planting inside degraded state forests.

projects.name: Orchard Juice
projects.excerpt:
Orchard Juice partners with farmers to grow fruit trees that restore depleted soils, using its harvest to make and sell freshly squeezed juice. In two years, the company has increased the number of farmers it engages with from 15,500 to 49,800.

This investment will support Orchard Juice’s existing efforts to plant more mango trees on smallholder farms and add exotic trees around the crops to protect them from strong winds. The funding will enable the company to promote agroforestry among farmers, showing them methods to sequester carbon and protect biodiversity while bringing in more profit.

projects.name: Association Rwandaise pour le Développement Endogène (ARDE/KUBAHO)
projects.excerpt:
ARDE/KUBAHO was established in 2007 with a vision to create self-reliant communities and better livelihoods throughout Rwanda. One of its four main areas of focus is environmental protection and sustainable agriculture.

With this grant from TerraFund, ARDE/KUBAHO will partner with smallholder farmers and local authorities on agroforestry projects across Rwanda’s Rubavu District, growing fruit and native trees on farmland and clumping bamboo on land affected by gullies.

projects.name: Institut d'Enseignement Superieur de Ruhengeri (INES-RUHENGERI)
projects.excerpt:
INES-RUHENGERI is an applied sciences institution in Rwanda’s Northern Province. Through different departments, it implements projects on environmental conservation, land management, and construction.

Through this grant, INES-RUHENGERI will work with Green Cover Initiative Rwanda, a non-profit organization that specializes in conducting technical trainings for farmers, to restore degraded landscapes in the mountainous Nkanka sector and Ishywa Island in Nkombo sector. By equipping farmers with the skills to set up nurseries and agroforestry systems, this work will enhance soil fertility and increase crop yields.

projects.name: African Evangelistic Enterprise (AEE-Rwanda)
projects.excerpt:
AEE Rwanda is a local Christian non-profit organization founded in 1984. With a focus on improving food security, AEE Rwanda partners with households and farmers to grow more crops for home use, local markets, and international exports.

AEE Rwanda will use this grant to rehabilitate communal lands and farms in the country’s Rutsiro and Rusizi Districts. Recognizing that agriculture is so central to this region, it will collaborate with farmers to establish small businesses that tap into the earning potential of agroforestry.

projects.name: BirdLife International - Kenya / Nature Rwanda
projects.excerpt:
Nature Rwanda’s vision is to build communities where human beings can coexist with nature without compromising the well-being of future generations. Through conservation projects, the organization looks to build climate resilience, reduce air pollution, and secure clean water for local residents.

With its second grant from TerraFund, Nature Rwanda is partnering with BirdLife International, a global partnership that strives to protect birds and their habitats worldwide. The two groups will work to revitalize Rwanda’s Butare and Bweyeye areas, where unsustainable agriculture and artisanal mining have eroded the soil.

projects.name: Association Protection des Ressources Naturelles pour le Bien-Etre de la Population au Burundi (APRN/BEPB)
projects.excerpt:
In 2019, 3C joined forces with (APRN/BEPB, a non-profit organization with over 20 years of experience in conservation, to create a consortium dedicated to advancing environmental protection in Burundi. To preserve the natural world – an important part of Burundi's heritage – the partnership aims to create a lasting place for it within the local economy.

This grant will allow the consortium to continue its work in the city of Bujumbura, where they will grow trees to protect the surrounding Ntahangwa and Nyabagere watersheds from further flooding and erosion. In addition to tree planting, the project will also include local education programs, nursery creation, and bushfire prevention.

projects.name: Rwanda Rural Rehabilitation Initiative (RWARRI)
projects.excerpt:
RWARRI is a non-profit organization in Rwanda with a mission to achieve sustainable livelihoods for low-income households. It partners with them to introduce income-generating activities like agroforestry, bee keeping and water harvesting. Over the last three years, the organization has grown about 2.3 million trees and engaged 308,000 community members in restoration projects.

RWARRI will use the grant to empower communities in Rutsiro and Rubavu and actively engage them in the restoration of the Lake Kivu catchment.

projects.name: Association pour le Développement Intégral des Communautés (ADIC)
projects.excerpt:
Starting in 2006, ADIC has employed a three-pronged “People, Planet, and Profit” approach to unite environmental protection, community capacity building, and sustainable income generation in Burundi. ADIC also partners with local government bodies to create co-management agreements for its projects, equitably distributing responsibility among community members.

ADIC will use this grant to promote modern farming techniques, advanced seed and plant varieties, and organic fertilizer among local farmers in the rural communities of Bubanza province. Over time, this work will increase crop yields and provide socioeconomic benefits for local households.

projects.name: Goshen Global Vision (GGV)
projects.excerpt:
Goshen Global Vision, a non-profit organization in Ghana's Western Region, aims to build resilience through community-based natural resource management and tree growing. The group works directly in the field with farmers, especially women and youth, to restore degraded land and forest reserves damaged by agricultural expansion. Goshen Global Vision has played a key role in establishing 38 village savings and loan associations, which serve as a platform to mobilize farmers for conservation and landscape restoration.

With this second grant from TerraFund, Goshen Global Vision will reforest degraded parts of the Subri Forest Reserve and grow biodiverse native trees among the cocoa farms of Ghana's Western Region.

projects.name: Hen Mpoano (Our Coast)
projects.excerpt:
Hen Mpoano, or Our Coast, is a Ghanaian non-profit organization that partners with local communities to sustainably manage coastal and marine ecosystems. In the past three years, Hen Mpoano has grown 153,000 trees and established more than 64 village savings and loan associations within Ghana’s coastal landscapes. The organization has also grown more than 900,000 mangroves through partnerships with several organizations and community members.

This second grant from TerraFund will help to expand restoration in the Greater Amanzule Wetland, building more resilient landscapes across Ghana’s southwestern coastline.

projects.name: Plate Forme Diobass au Kivu
projects.excerpt:
Since its creation in 1996, Plateforme Diobass au Kivu has sought to facilitate knowledge sharing between Congolese and international groups. The organization is one branch within the Diobass network across Africa, with an approach that emphasizes community-based solutions to social and economic problems, cultural values, and local resources.

Plateforme Diobass au Kivu will use this grant to revitalize the slopes of Kamanyola groupement and develop sustainable agricultural value chains to secure farming households’ incomes. It will also develop agricultural and apicultural value chains to benefit target households in the Walungu territory.

projects.name: Réseau Burundi 2000 Plus
projects.excerpt:
Réseau Burundi 2000 Plus aims to improve the livelihoods of farming families through technical and financial support. Working under multiple themes, such as community health, job creation, and long-term environmental protection, the group supports communities in the Gihanga commune of Bubanza Province.

Using this grant from TerraFund, Réseau Burundi 2000 Plus will use agroforestry, reforestation to restore smallholder farmers’ land and riparian areas in Bubanza Province. By growing more crops and securing a reliable food supply, the organization will fight malnutrition among schoolchildren.

projects.name: Emfed Farms and Trading Company
projects.excerpt:
Emfed Farms is an agricultural services company founded in Ghana in 2012. It provides full-farm management services to smallholder cocoa farmers who cannot take care of their land or pay upfront management costs. The business improves soil fertility, eliminates pests, and strengthens existing cocoa trees by pruning, composting and planting other tree species that provide shade.

Investment from TerraFund will bolster Emfed’s efforts to plant tree species that provide ecosystem services and support biodiversity. The company's agroforestry practices will reduce soil erosion, retain water, and boost economic vitality in the process.

projects.name: Association pour la Promotion des Cultures Vivrières (APROCUVI)
projects.excerpt:
Since 2002, APROCUVI has demonstrated a long-standing commitment to revitalizing Burundi’s landscapes. With a focus on women and youth, APROCUVI supports farmers in crop management and processing, develops marketing for producers, and provides training and education to cooperatives.

While APROCUVI works across the entire country, this grant will be used to restore the base of the Murangara-Ruramata mountains, a region consistently threatened by periods of both drought and flooding. Local communities will co-manage this project, lowering food insecurity, bolstering their incomes, and reducing the risk of soil erosion in the process.

projects.name: Goshen Farm Exporters
projects.excerpt:
Goshen Farm Exporters creates businesses opportunities for smallholder farmers by processing surplus tropical fruits into premium snacks. The company’s restoration efforts promote responsible sourcing, providing resilient seedlings to its network of farming partners. Goshen’s ultimate mission is to create an inclusive market for over 4,800 smallholder farmers in rural southeastern and coastal Kenya while minimizing food loss.

This investment will help Goshen introduce and plant diverse varieties of mango trees, provide biofertilizer to regenerate the soil, and create sustainable incomes for farmers in Kenya’s Makueni County.

projects.name: Plant with Purpose
projects.excerpt:
Plant with Purpose is a Christian non-profit organization formed in 1984. It has partnered with over 81,000 smallholder farming families in nine countries to reverse the impacts of deforestation: Burundi, the DRC, the Dominican Republic, Ethiopia, Haiti, Mexico, Tanzania, and Thailand.

With this second grant from TerraFund, Plant with Purpose’s local affiliate Floresta Burundi will spearhead tree growing in the provinces of Bujumbura and Bururi. It will also teach farmers to make energy-saving stoves, clearing the air in their homes and reducing the need for firewood.

projects.name: World Wide Fund for Nature - Kenya (WWF-Kenya)
projects.excerpt:
WWF-Kenya is a Kenyan non-governmental conservation organization, and an affiliate of WWF International. With 60 years of experience in Kenya, the organization has worked with local communities, the government, private sector organizations and civil society to conserve the environment – and has grown nearly 3,000,000 trees over the last three years.

With the TerraFund grant, WWF-Kenya will train farmers to build “farm forests” across Nyandarua, growing high-value trees that put money right in the pocket of local community members. The organization will also bring its significant technical and monitoring support to the project, ensuring that impact is carefully measured.

projects.name: Farmlife Health Services
projects.excerpt:
Farmlife Health Services is dedicated to empowering smallholder farmers through climate-smart agriculture, sustainable land restoration, and value addition, with a strong focus on improving livelihoods, food security, and resilience to climate change. With four years of experience, the organization has built a reputation for innovative approaches, robust community partnerships, and facilitating access to premium markets. Farmlife has demonstrated success in reducing post-harvest losses, increasing farm-gate prices, and supporting farmers—especially women and youth—through training, financial inclusion, and the development of nature-based enterprises.

The proposed project will restore degraded smallholder farmlands in Nakuru County, specifically across the Mau East escarpment in areas such as Njoro, Likia, Mauche, and Teret. The initiative aims to establish 200,000 native and fruit trees over 400 hectares, blending agroforestry with native forest restoration to improve soil fertility, water retention, and biodiversity. Activities include high-quality seedling production, community training in climate-smart practices, and the development of value chains for avocados, honey, and other nature-based enterprises. The project will engage over 1,000 farmers—most of whom are women and youth—through capacity building, employment, and financial services, while ensuring high tree survival rates through structured maintenance and monitoring. By strengthening riparian buffers and supporting local stewardship, the project seeks to deliver lasting ecological recovery and economic resilience for the region.

projects.name: Rwanda Environmental Conservation Organization (RECOR)
projects.excerpt:
For over 20 years, RECOR has partnered with local leaders and community members to find sustainable environmental solutions that benefit people across Rwanda.

RECOR will use its second TerraFund grant to restore the degraded shores and upper lands of Lake Kivu, protecting water supply and biodiversity. They will also promote agroforestry among farmers by providing them with grafted fruit trees and organic compost, which will improve soil quality and increase crop yields.

projects.name: The Rural Development Interdiocesan Service (RDIS)
projects.excerpt:
The Rural Development Interdiocesan Service (RDIS) is a Rwandan NGO established by five Anglican dioceses, with a mission to safeguard the environment and promote sustainable, holistic community development. With over a decade of experience, RDIS has built a strong reputation for advancing environmental protection through landscape restoration, climate-smart agriculture, and socio-economic empowerment. The organization operates through a network of field offices and skilled staff, engaging local leaders and community facilitators to deliver inclusive, community-based projects. RDIS is recognized for its institutional maturity and effective coordination, empowering rural smallholder farmers with training, technical support, and resources to improve livelihoods and environmental outcomes.

The proposed project aims to restore 389 hectares of degraded land in Rusizi District by planting 300,000 trees and introducing soil-fixing grasses to reduce erosion, with a target of 240,000 surviving trees by 2031. The initiative will enhance biodiversity, improve water quality, and increase agricultural productivity for 1,200 smallholder households, while creating 255 green jobs through nursery operations, tree planting, and community monitoring. Activities include establishing community nurseries, training trainers and farmers in agroecological practices, distributing fruit seedlings, setting up demonstration plots, and supporting beekeeping enterprises for income diversification. The project is fully community-led, involving local authorities, cooperatives, women and youth groups, and ensures long-term sustainability through participatory site selection, ongoing maintenance, and robust monitoring systems. By 2031, the project expects to achieve significant improvements in food security, ecosystem connectivity, and rural livelihoods in Rusizi District.

projects.name: Green Belt Movement (GBM)
projects.excerpt:
GBM is an environmental organization in Kenya that empowers communities, especially women, to conserve the environment and improve livelihoods. It was founded by Professor Wangari Maathai in 1977 under the auspices of the National Council of Women of Kenya to respond to the needs of rural women dealing with the consequences of environmental degradation.

This grant will support restoration projects in Kenya’s Mau East Forest that increase species diversity, empower communities to increase household incomes by growing trees with high economic value, and secure life-giving water for the area.

projects.name: Unissons-Nous pour la Promotion des Batwa (UNIPROBA)
projects.excerpt:
Founded in 1999, UNIPROBA is dedicated to improving the livelihoods and political representation of the Indigenous Batwa community in Burundi, all while safeguarding the natural environment. They protect the biodiverse Kibira National Park from degradation and work with Batwa communities to plant fruit trees in the Kirundo and Bujumbura provinces.

UNIPROBA will use its TerraFund grant to improve livelihoods, reinforce the climate resilience of marginalized households, and restore the Nyamitanga and Kaburantwa hills to prosperity.

projects.name: Albertine Rift Conservation Society (ARCOS Network)
projects.excerpt:
With this funding, FCPEEP and the ARCOS Network are partnering on new project to reforest the Luiro River watershed in the DRC. By growing trees along the riverbank, the two organizations will reduce the area’s vulnerability to landslides.

FCPEEP, a non-profit environmental protection organization from the DRC, will lead implementation and design learning case studies to evaluate the impacts of this work. ARCOS will provide support by training FCPEEP representatives in its BEST approach, a system that aims to build leadership, enhance environmental resilience, foster sustainable businesses, and inspire others through nature-based villages.

projects.name: Y & M Regeneration
projects.excerpt:
Y&M Regeneration is a women-led company in Ghana that produces timber and tree crop seedlings for plantations, agroforestry systems, and forest restoration projects. Since founding its first nursery in 2009, the company has supplied seedlings that have been planted across over 1,000 hectares, built several new nurseries, and grown a variety of agricultural products for sale on the market, including cashews and corn.

The investment will support the company’s Ecocert certification for honey products and its efforts to increase forest cover through tree planting, intercropping, and beekeeping.

projects.name: Herp-Ghana
projects.excerpt:
Herp-Ghana advocates for reptile and amphibian conservation within Ghanaian communities. Its mission is to establish new protected areas and restore priority habitats that benefit people and safeguard these species.

This second grant from TerraFund will equip Herp-Ghana to restore degraded forests within the Wenchi Municipality. The project will offer employment opportunities for over 100 women and youth and improve the livelihoods of the town’s farmers.

projects.name: Organisation de Défense de l'Environnement et le Développement Durable (ODEB)
projects.excerpt:
ODEB is a nonprofit operating in 9 communities in Burundi’s Bubanza Province. Using adaptable and community-based solutions, the organization’s mission is to protect the sustainable management of natural resources within the region. With two guiding principles, urgency and sustainable development, its interventions address water quality, hygiene and sanitation, food security, climate adaptation, and community well-being.

With this grant, ODEB will partner with farmers to restore the banks of the Rusizi River. By planting mango, papaya, and other fruit trees to hold the soil in place, the group will prevent contaminants from flowing into the water. The group will also carry out agroforestry and woodlot interventions.

projects.name: Prime Biodiversity Conservation (PBC)
projects.excerpt:
Founded by a group of passionate conservationists in 2018, PBC is dedicated to protecting the rich biodiversity of Rwanda and beyond. Over the last five years, PBC has educated young people on how to embrace environmental conservation practices like growing trees and caring for saplings in nurseries.

PBC will use this grant to grow native trees with children in schools and at home with their families. It will also hold capacity building sessions to empower schools and communities to create, manage and own tree nurseries. This work will take place in the Rubavu and Rutsiro districts.

projects.name: Rural Development Initiative (RDI)
projects.excerpt: Rural Development Initiative (RDI) is a youth- and sustainable agriculture-focused NGO dedicated to empowering rural communities by promoting environmentally responsible practices and improving livelihoods. With seven years of experience, RDI has built a strong reputation for transforming subsistence farming into market-oriented agriculture, providing training, and connecting smallholder farmers to markets. The organization is recognized for its community-driven approach, capacity building, and successful delivery of restoration projects, particularly those that integrate gender and youth inclusion. RDI’s mission centers on equipping the poorest communities with the tools and knowledge needed for sustainable income generation and resilience. The proposed project aims to restore degraded land and enhance community livelihoods in the Boneza sector of Rutsiro District through large-scale tree planting, job creation, and inclusive community engagement. RDI will plant 250,000 trees across 285 hectares to boost biodiversity, soil fertility, and water conservation, while also renovating banana and passion fruit plantations to increase food security and income. The initiative will create 500 jobs, prioritizing women and youth, and establish six community savings and loan groups to promote financial inclusion. Activities include site selection with local authorities, nursery establishment, community training, and ongoing maintenance and monitoring by agronomists and local champions. The project emphasizes sustainability through regular follow-ups, technical support, and the use of digital tools for tracking progress, aiming to directly benefit 4,000 people and indirectly reach 8,000, ultimately strengthening climate resilience and community well-being in Boneza.

projects.name: Tropenbos Ghana Programme (TBG)
projects.excerpt:
Established in 2001, Tropenbos Ghana brings knowledge from its international network of experts and community leaders to transform landscapes. In Ghana, it restores the Juabeso-Bia and Sefwi-Wiawso landscapes, where cocoa farms have expanded into natural forests, threatening biodiversity and the long-term health and prosperity of farming communities.

A grant from TerraFund will help Tropenbos Ghana empower communities to grow trees in degraded forests across the Asante Akim South Municipal of the Ashanti Region.

projects.name: Communities of Hope
projects.excerpt:
Founded 10 years ago in Burundi, Communities of Hope transforms landscapes and lives by providing low-income families with land, seeds and other forms of support for sustainable living. The organization has engaged 36,000 community members in their activities over the last three years and grown 120,000 trees.

Communities of Hope will use this grant to restore land in Burundi’s Bubanza and Cibitoke Provinces by expanding agroforestry, silvopasture and reforestation around Kibira National Park. This area, long degraded by slash-and-burn agriculture and excessive logging, will start to see a greener future.

projects.name: Conservation Cocoa Association
projects.excerpt:
Conservation Cocoa Association is a well-established organization with over a decade of experience in environmental restoration, climate change mitigation, and community empowerment. Their mission centers on solving environmental challenges, promoting sustainable land use, and advocating for the rights of marginalized rural communities. With a strong track record in forest landscape restoration and environmental awareness, they have demonstrated institutional capacity and a commitment to integrating local communities into conservation efforts.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded forest landscapes in the Bia West district by establishing nurseries of native tree species for afforestation and implementing agroforestry practices with indigenous timber species and assisted natural regeneration across ten communities. The initiative will build the capacity of 300 off-reserve farmers in sustainable forest and agroforest management, develop alternative livelihoods in the target communities, and monitor ecological, social, and economic outcomes of the restored areas. Activities include stakeholder engagement, site assessment, nursery establishment, tree planting, alternative livelihood development, and ongoing maintenance and evaluation to ensure long-term ecosystem health and community benefits. The project emphasizes ecological restoration while supporting local livelihoods, though it could further enhance functional diversity by incorporating multi-purpose native species.

projects.name: Kula Project
projects.excerpt:
Kula Project’s mission is to eradicate poverty by empowering entrepreneurs in Rwanda's smallholder coffee communities. Through its Kula Fellowship, the group partners with primarily women coffee farmers to provide agronomy training, financial investment, and one-on-one mentorship. After entering the program, participants have seen their coffee yields double and tripled their household incomes.

Kula will use this TerraFund grant to provide coffee and shade trees to a community of approximately 1,500 smallholder coffee farmers in the Nyamasheke District of Rwanda’s Western Province.

projects.name: Action pour la Protection de l'Environnement et la Promotion des Filières Agricoles (APEFA)
projects.excerpt:
Established in 2008, APEFA aims to build resilient farming systems and long-lasting food security in Rwanda. The group focuses on giving vulnerable communities the knowledge and tools that they need.

With this grant, APEFA will work to restore and protect the banks and watersheds of the Rusizi River. By training local farmers to grow bamboo, silky oak, and fruit trees among their crops, the organization will improve water quality for all who live near the river basin.

projects.name: Moto Feeds
projects.excerpt:
Moto Feeds collaborates with local Maasai pastoralist communities in Kenya to rejuvenate degraded grasslands through affordable fodder solutions. In partnership with the Maasai, the company grows a highly nutritious and rapidly regenerating grass for animal feed and provides an all-season soil cover known as Boma Rhodes grass. This contributes to the community's financial well-being, as its members can also sell surplus grass bales for income.

This investment will enable Moto Feeds to establish its first tree nurseries in Nakuru and Narok Counties, expanding its business model and accelerating production to make more saplings available for purchase.

projects.name: Organization for Support to the Environmental Protection and Climate Change Adaptation (OSEPCCA)
projects.excerpt:
OSEPCCA builds partnerships with government and private institutions to implement landscape restoration, environmental protection, and food security projects in Rwanda.

With this grant, the group will work with farmers and communities across the district of Rutsiro to restore depleted croplands, woodlots, and river networks. OSEPCCA will focus on propagating native seedlings that are favored by the local community. These plants, well-suited to the local soil and climate, are more likely to thrive and will lower the risk of invasive species taking over the ecosystem.

projects.name: Rural Environmental and Development Organization (REDO)
projects.excerpt:
Founded in 1999, REDO is a Rwandan non-profit organization that works with local communities to earn a living while also working towards environmental conservation. These include disseminating improved stoves that use less energy, tree planting, bee keeping, water harvesting and soil conservation.

With this grant, REDO will construct tree nurseries and engage the local community in growing trees to revitalize Lake Kivu Catchment in the Rusizi District. It will adopt the BEST approach of Rwandan conservation group ARCOS Network to build leadership, enhance environmental resilience, start sustainable businesses, and transform communities.

projects.name: Eden Reforestation Projects
projects.excerpt:
Eden Reforestation Projects is a global organization that strives to cultivate healthy relationships between people and the forests they depend on. Since 2004, Eden has scaled its restoration programming to bring an estimated 76,000 hectares of degraded forest land under active restoration around the globe. It began working in Kenya in 2019 and now operates throughout the country in both its mangrove and afromontane forest landscapes.

This funding will allow Eden to expand work on its oldest restoration site in the Mau Forest, Ol Mariko. With local communities at the lead, the project will enhance forest connectivity to attract diverse wildlife and create a more vibrant ecosystem.

projects.name: A Rocha Ghana (ARG)
projects.excerpt:
A Rocha Ghana has dedicated itself to preserving the Earth’s sustainable resources since 1999. With four project offices spread out across the country, the organization’s objective is to inspire and empower people to care for nature, while promoting and supporting sustainable natural resource management.

The organization is committed to developing its own institutional capacity as well the capacity of its collaborating partners and to provide services and networking opportunities for conservation of important ecological habitats.

A Rocha Ghana will use this grant to restore the rapidly dwindling Atewa Forest, training women and youth to cultivate saplings and working with cocoa farmers to grow trees across their crops.

projects.name: Ecological Nest
projects.excerpt:
Ecological Nest is a conservation-focused organization based in Accra, dedicated to promoting the sustainable use of natural resources and supporting communities that depend on nature. With a decade of experience, the organization emphasizes science-driven restoration, strategic partnerships, and community engagement. Guided by a five-member board led by a respected conservation scientist, Ecological Nest operates under a five-year strategy that prioritizes ecorestoration. Their work is informed by research and collaboration with local stakeholders, and they have a track record of integrating conservation actions with community needs to achieve lasting environmental and social benefits.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded areas along the Bia River Tributaries, focusing on improving ecosystem services, biodiversity, and local livelihoods. Ecological Nest will work with 300 farmers from Agyeikrom, Old Papase, Papase, and Pioga to implement agroforestry practices, restore 180 hectares of riparian and cocoa landscapes, and enhance water quality along 1.8 km of the river. Activities include community engagement, nursery establishment, seedling raising, land preparation, tree planting, and ongoing maintenance, with a strong emphasis on native species and watershed restoration. The project will also support off-farm livelihoods such as beekeeping and avocado cultivation, and train communities in monitoring techniques using mobile apps and citizen science. By project end, the initiative expects to improve water quality, increase cocoa yields, and boost farmer incomes through restoration-related employment and sustainable land management.

projects.name: Solidaridad - East and Central Africa
projects.excerpt:
Recognizing how farmers in developing countries struggle to access markets, Solidaridad partners with communities to improve value chains and find sustainable markets for their produce.

The TerraFund grant will expand its “Shade 4 Vegetables” (SAVE) project, which restore degraded catchments using agroforestry systems. Solidaridad will partner with small-scale farmers in Laikipia and Nyandarua counties to integrate trees in vegetable farming systems adjacent to the catchment and broader watershed to improve water security in this dry region.

projects.name: Biodiversity Conservation Organization (BIOCOOR)
projects.excerpt:
BIOCOOR is a youth-led non-profit organization in Rwanda. Focusing on the districts surrounding Nyungwe National Park, the group is dedicated to conserving biodiversity, promoting ecotourism, improving community health, and mitigating climate change.

BIOCOOR will use this grant to revitalize Rwanda’s Nyamasheke district with native tree species. In a region afflicted by declining crop yields, this project will create job opportunities in tree growing, agroforestry, and ecotourism.

projects.name: GROOTS Kenya Association
projects.excerpt: Established in 1995, GROOTS Kenya is a women-led non-profit organization that addresses the lack of visibility of grassroots women in processes that affect their lives. The group uses a bottom-up model that places women at the center of decision-making, allowing them to take charge of their own development. It works with over 1,500 women farmers in restoration by encouraging sustainable farming and agroforestry. With this grant, GROOTS Kenya will increase climate and food resilience for communities in four landscapes within Kenya’s Baringo and Laikipia Counties. This will involve growing trees with local groups and other partners to mitigate the area’s constant hot and dry conditions.

projects.name: Association pour la Promotion de l'Agriculture de Conservation et de Protection de l'Environnement (PACPE)
projects.excerpt:
"PACPE is a community-focused organization with eight years of experience at the intersection of rural development, food security, and ecological restoration. Its mission centers on sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, reforestation, and agroforestry on degraded lands, with a strong emphasis on gender equity and community empowerment. PACPE employs participatory and adaptive approaches, co-designing projects with local communities and valuing traditional knowledge. The organization has a proven track record, having restored thousands of hectares and planted millions of trees through partnerships with international donors and government agencies. Its work has led to increased vegetation cover, improved biodiversity, enhanced food security, and strengthened local governance structures, directly benefiting thousands of households.

The proposed project aims to restore 410 hectares of degraded land on the Mugeru sub-hill of Nyempundu through participatory reforestation, agroforestry, and the protection of endemic species. By engaging 250 households—at least 60% women and youth—the project will establish two community nurseries to produce 184,000 seedlings, reforest 40 hectares with native and exotic species, and promote agroforestry on 370 hectares of farmland. Activities include training households in planting and maintenance, forming local monitoring committees, and creating two farmer field schools to build agroecological skills. The project will also develop fruit value chains and create 320 jobs, aiming to increase biodiversity, reduce soil erosion, and improve water availability. Community-driven planning and ongoing training will ensure the survival and ecological impact of planted trees, while local governance structures will support long-term maintenance and benefits for the community."

projects.name: Community Socio-Environmental Organization (COSEO)
projects.excerpt:
Since its establishment in 2005, COSEO has cultivated over 5 million saplings in the rolling hills of Kenya’s Baringo County. The organization’s expertise also lies in bamboo seedlings, which it has sold and donated for planting within degraded sections of the Lembus Forest watershed.

With this grant, COSEO will carry out a degradation survey and develop a restoration plan for the Lembus Forest. By controlling soil erosion with trees and bamboo, the group will protect the streams that feed into the nearby Lake Baringo, a vital water source for the Greater Rift Valley.

projects.name: Laikipia Wildlife Forum (LWF)
projects.excerpt:
LWF supports conservation efforts and natural resource management initiatives in the Laikipia region of Kenya’s Greater Rift Valley. Its mission is to nurture and support stakeholder institutions that champion wildlife conservation and sustainable natural resource management.

With this grant, LWF will restore wildlife habitats in the Upper Ewaso Ng'iro Basin through reforestation, agroforestry, silvopasture and assisted natural regeneration. The new forest corridors will provide a safe home for elephants, monkeys, and leopards.

projects.name: Paran Women Group
projects.excerpt:
In 2005, a group of Indigenous women in Ololulunga, a village in Kenya’s Narok County, formed Paran Women Group to involve their peers in tree growing and re-greening projects. The organization has worked with marginalized communities in the Mau Forest by educating them about Indigenous rights, training them on forest conservation, and providing energy efficient cookstoves to cut their reliance on firewood for cooking fuel.

Paran Women Group will use this grant to share tree planting and environmental conservation practices with the local community, encouraging them to protect the Mau Forest and its nearby farms.

projects.name: Leona Foundation
projects.excerpt:
Leona Foundation seeks to promote community transformation in Kenya, collaborating with marginalized groups to safeguard the environment. The organization has partnered with several community forest associations to carry out restoration projects, impacting more than 300,000 members within the Mau Forest ecosystem. Over the last three years, the organization has grown 646,000 trees and restored 804 hectares of land.

Leona Foundation will use this funding to revitalize the Bahati Forest, protect biodiversity hotspots, promote natural regeneration in areas with mild degradation, and support community-based forest scouting and surveillance.

projects.name: Rwanda Organic Agriculture Movement (ROAM)
projects.excerpt:
For years, members of Rwanda's organic agriculture industry, including farmers, processors, and exporters, faced limited avenues to showcase their products. In 2007, ROAM was established to provide an organized and more focused movement dedicated to promoting organic agriculture. It is a member of the International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movement (IFOAM), a global umbrella organization for organic agriculture movements that represents nearly 800 affiliates in 117 countries.

With this grant, ROAM will spearhead forest restoration initiatives, encompassing tree growing, natural resources management, and agriculture in Rutsiro District, alongside other community-led tree-growing endeavors.

projects.name: Women in Water and Natural Resources Conservation (WWANC)
projects.excerpt:
Women in Water and Natural Resources Conservation (WWANC) is a women-led organization dedicated to empowering women and girls through sustainable community development, with a strong emphasis on climate resilience, conservation, and restoration. With over a decade of experience, WWANC has established itself as a leader in participatory, women-centered approaches to environmental stewardship, equipping grassroots women with the knowledge and skills to protect ecosystems and drive positive change. The organization is recognized for its robust governance, community engagement, and commitment to gender-responsive restoration, consistently fostering partnerships that prioritize long-term, inclusive solutions.

The proposed project focuses on restoring the Sururu Forest and adjacent riparian areas by conserving endangered species, enhancing native tree cover, and improving hydrological functions. WWANC will co-plant indigenous seedlings in the forest, watershed, and agroforestry systems, rehabilitate riparian buffer zones, and implement upstream tributary restoration to support ecosystem health and water quality. The initiative also aims to improve local livelihoods and reduce pressure on forest resources by distributing energy-saving cookstoves and agroforestry trees, including fruit trees, to the community. Targeted income-generating activities and leadership opportunities will promote socio-economic equity, particularly for women, youth, and marginalized groups in the Sururu forest catchment. The project will be implemented through community mobilization, baseline assessments, site preparation, planting, and ongoing maintenance and monitoring, ensuring active local participation and sustainable impact.

projects.name: Rwanda Climate Change and Development Network (RCCDN)
projects.excerpt:
The Rwanda Climate Change and Development Network (RCCDN) leads a consortium with RBI and REAO, combining expertise in environmental management, community engagement, and sustainable livelihoods. RCCDN oversees coordination, financial management, and reporting, leveraging its experience in managing large-scale restoration projects, including planting over 1.2 million trees and restoring 3,500 hectares. The consortium operates with robust systems for monitoring, evaluation, and stakeholder engagement, and has a proven track record in promoting gender and disability inclusion. RBI and REAO contribute field-level restoration, community mobilization, and capacity building, with notable achievements in tree planting, household support, and environmental education, enhancing the consortium’s ability to deliver impactful restoration and community resilience initiatives.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded landscapes through large-scale agroforestry and fruit tree planting, targeting the establishment and maintenance of 202,000 trees and the sustained growth of at least 169,000 trees. The initiative will improve soil fertility, reduce erosion, conserve water resources, and promote sustainable land management, directly benefiting over 574 households by integrating restoration with food security and economic empowerment. Activities include community mobilization, nursery establishment, hands-on training in restoration techniques, and ongoing monitoring using GIS tools. The project emphasizes community ownership, with local leaders and trained members managing nurseries and tree care, while dedicated field officers and M&E experts ensure high survival rates and adaptive management. By focusing on practical, community-driven restoration and capacity building, the project seeks to enhance ecosystem health, climate resilience, and household livelihoods in the targeted area.

projects.name: Horizon Business Ventures (HBV)
projects.excerpt:
Horizon Business Ventures (HBV) is a Kenyan company with eight years of experience in sustainable enterprise, focusing on essential oils production that integrates biodiversity, business, and community wellbeing. HBV’s mission is to provide high-quality, eco-friendly products while promoting economic and environmental sustainability in rural areas. The organization is recognized for its commitment to ethical sourcing, social impact, and fostering positive ecological change, positioning itself as a trusted brand that balances consumer health with environmental stewardship.

The proposed project will restore 130 hectares of degraded land in Marmanet Forest and nearby farmlands through community-led reforestation and agroforestry. HBV will partner with local community groups and farmers to raise and plant 110,000 trees, with a focus on regenerating native species and valuable shrubs for essential oil extraction. The initiative includes training over 300 households in sustainable harvesting and marketing of non-wood forest products, integrating agroforestry to protect the forest and enhance farm productivity. The project’s workplan involves establishing nurseries, preparing sites, phased tree planting, and developing complementary livelihoods such as beekeeping and eco-tourism. Ongoing community-driven maintenance and monitoring will ensure high tree survival rates and long-term ecosystem health, while HBV’s processing facility in Nanyuki will create market incentives for conservation. The project aims to improve climate resilience, biodiversity, and local livelihoods, offering a scalable model for nature-based enterprise and restoration.

projects.name: Pan African Climate Justice Alliance (PACJA)
projects.excerpt:
PACJA is a consortium of more than 1,000 organizations from 48 African countries. The alliance brings its members together over a shared vision: a people-centered, rights-based approach to address the environmental challenges facing humanity.

With this grant, PACJA will work with local communities to rehabilitate the degraded lands of Kenya’s West Pokot County. The group will train community members to establish and maintain tree nurseries, ensuring a steady supply of seedlings for reforestation.

projects.name: Itombwe Génération pour l'Humanité (IGH)
projects.excerpt:
IGH is a non-profit organization in the DRC. Its main mission is to protect the biodiversity and forest habitat of the Itombwe Mountains, which run west of the Rusizi River Basin. Since its establishment in 2014, the organization has involved more than 7,000 local community members through forestry committee training programs.

IGH will use its grant from TerraFund to increase forest cover in South Kivu Province and improve food security by working with farmers to grow trees among their crops.

projects.name: Ogiek Peoples' Development Program (OPDP)
projects.excerpt:
OPDP is a Kenya-based non-profit organization founded in 1999. Led by elders, thought leaders, and professionals from the Ogiek Indigenous community, the group was formed in the wake of historical injustices that stripped the population of their land rights. OPDP’s work centers on promoting Ogiek culture, securing community participation in all sectors, championing land rights, and advocating for sustainable development.

This grant will enable OPDP to revitalize the Mau Forest by increasing tree cover, fostering sustainable livelihood projects among forest groups, and enhancing community members’ knowledge of forest conservation strategies.

projects.name: Plant-for-the-Planet Ghana
projects.excerpt:
Plant-for-the-Planet Ghana is dedicated to restoring degraded landscapes, combating climate change, and empowering local communities through tree planting and sustainable land use. With five years of experience, the organization has established a strong track record in ecological restoration, focusing on community nurseries, agroforestry, and inclusive engagement of youth and women. Their approach combines science-based methods with community-driven initiatives, training, and partnerships, ensuring long-term sustainability and impact. Notably, their affiliation with the global Plant-for-the-Planet network strengthens their capacity and donor base, while their financial independence and innovative strategies, such as solar-powered nurseries, position them as leaders in restoration efforts.

The proposed project aims to restore 150 hectares of degraded forest in the Bosomtwe Range Forest Reserve and surrounding areas by planting 140,000 native and agroforestry trees over two years, with four additional years of aftercare. The initiative integrates ecological restoration with livelihood development, supplying cocoa and fruit trees to local farmers, establishing a managed woodlot for sustainable charcoal, and supporting income-generating activities like honey production, aquaculture, and grasscutter rearing—prioritizing women and youth. A solar-powered nursery will provide seedlings for this and future projects, reducing long-term costs and supporting ongoing restoration. The project will work closely with community cooperatives and the Forestry Commission to map sites, create firebreaks, and ensure effective monitoring and maintenance, ultimately enhancing biodiversity, soil health, water security, and community resilience in the Bosomtwe area.

projects.name: Youth in Agroecology and Business Learning Track Africa (YALTA)
projects.excerpt: Youth in Agroecology and Business Learning Track Africa (YALTA) Rwanda is dedicated to empowering youth and women to restore degraded landscapes through agroecological innovation. With four years of experience, YALTA has established itself as a leader in combining restoration with entrepreneurship, capacity building, and inclusive governance. The organization’s mission centers on transforming degraded areas into climate-resilient, productive ecosystems, ensuring that biodiversity recovery is closely linked to food security and rural prosperity. YALTA’s track record includes successful partnerships and community engagement, particularly in mobilizing local actors and fostering sustainable land management practices. The proposed project aims to restore degraded land and strengthen livelihoods in Rusizi District by integrating agroforestry, regenerative agriculture, and community-led governance. Over six years, YALTA will restore 400 hectares by planting and nurturing a diverse mix of indigenous, fruit, and multipurpose trees, directly benefiting 170 households. The initiative will enhance food and income security through agroforestry on terraces and farms, improve watershed health by reducing erosion, and develop climate-resilient value chains such as fruit, vegetables, and honey. Community capacity will be built through Farmer Field Schools, youth agroecology clubs, and restoration committees, ensuring strong local ownership and governance. The project emphasizes participatory land mapping, nursery establishment, large-scale planting, ongoing maintenance, and robust monitoring using digital tools, with a focus on youth and women’s involvement. By project end, the initiative expects to achieve high tree survival rates, improved watershed services, diversified livelihoods, and strengthened community governance in Rusizi District.

projects.name: Sustainable Agroforestry Initiative (SAFI)
projects.excerpt: This proposed project will focus planting activities for the first 2-years and continue monitoring the project for the next 3-years to ensure planted trees are well established and free to grow from competing weeds. Our restoration implementation activities are determined and designed through series of education, town hall meetings, focus group discussion and baseline study involving the local people and the traditional authorities. The local people must agree to stop uncontrolled fire, agree to help plant and manage the trees, and agree to share the revenue. The traditional authorities, the custodians of the land must agree to allocate land for planting. Both activities are developed by the local people so that a fair and transparent system set up to share the revenue. Our implementation stages involve community mobilization, registration of the local people, training and recruitment of seasonal and part-time workers from the local community for nursery construction and management. We contract local famers to engage in seed collection. This is followed by site selection, demarcation and preparation. We engage the local people to manually prepare the planting sites. We supported with cutlasses, axes, hoes, protecting gears, transportation, food and water. After land preparation, we conduct pegging and planting of seedlings. We generally use 3m X 3m planting spacing. After planting, we conduct tree survival assessment. During this stage, we replace all the dead trees. Fires and competing weeds are major threats to planted trees. We maintain the planted trees by managing weeds and fires and occasional grazing. We manage weeds by supporting local people to manually clear their planting sites twice in a year. We recruit, train and contract local people to form community fire management advisory group. This group control, prevent, monitor and suppress fire activities during the dry season when wildfires are very active. We established fire-belts along the plantation boundary. We become part of the community and make our presence well established through project implementation. Our field officers live in the communities and provide day-to-day management and monitoring of implementation activities. The project monitoring team routinely conduct field monitoring once every month. Every six month, the project manager engages with the field officers to discuss the monitoring report and provide solutions to any implementation challenges.

projects.name: The Big Thunder Mining Company
projects.excerpt:
The Big Thunder Mining Company is dedicated to sustainable macadamia processing and community-driven environmental restoration. With five years of experience, the organization has established itself as a leader in promoting traceability, empowering farming communities, and advancing reforestation efforts. Their operations include processing high-quality macadamia kernels for export, upcycling shells into biomass energy, and producing premium cosmetic oil from grade B kernels. Big Thunder’s commitment to sustainability is reflected in their support for farmer registration, distribution of tree seedlings, and the creation of local jobs, particularly for women and youth.

The proposed project aims to restore approximately 625 hectares of degraded land by distributing 110,000 macadamia seedlings and 15,000 indigenous seedlings to contracted farmers, enhancing both biodiversity and livelihoods. A 1-acre nursery will be established to supply seedlings, employing local women and youth and sourcing inputs locally to stimulate the economy. The project will engage communities through training in nursery management, agroforestry, and aftercare, with farmer groups signing agreements to ensure accountability. Continuous monitoring and technical support will be provided by an extension team and agronomist to achieve a high tree survival rate. Strategically located buying and aggregation centers will be set up to improve market access and traceability, while investments in processing infrastructure will support increased production. The initiative is expected to deliver environmental benefits such as improved biodiversity and soil health, create jobs, and strengthen the macadamia value chain in the region.

projects.name: Mission of Hope for Society International Foundation (MIHOSO International)
projects.excerpt:
MIHOSO International is committed to building a safe world for women, youth, and children. It carries out social development programs across seven regions in Ghana, working with over 1,000 communities to improve their well-being.

With this funding, MIHOSO will conduct a baseline survey in forest fringe and cocoa-growing communities to determine the underlying causes of degradation and its impacts on local residents. The organization also plans to train smallholder cocoa farmers and youth on sustainable agriculture and show them how to cultivate non-timber forest products.

projects.name: Sakam Savana
projects.excerpt:
Sakam Savana is a Ghanaian company that grows commercial trees and facilitates agroforestry on smallholder farms. Its mission is to improve economic livelihoods for rural communities residing on the outskirts of degraded forests while also protecting their water sources.

This investment will enable Sakam Savana to revitalize a watershed in Afram Headwaters Forest Reserve, tying water conservation and land restoration together. Through this project, the company will restore ecosystem services that have been depleted by logging and farmland expansion. These benefits will be shared between the company, the forestry commission, and the local community, who can also use the newly restored area to gather plants for medicinal purposes and fish.

projects.name: Unis pour l'Education Socioenvironnementale de la Femme (UESEF)
projects.excerpt:
UESEF is a Congolese nonprofit whose vision is to provide environmental education, economic opportunities, and improved livelihoods to women and young people. They restore forest and aquatic ecosystems by promoting climate-smart agriculture and bolstering women’s involvement in natural resource management and access to social and health services.

UESEF will use its TerraFund grant to restore trees to the landscape, provide technical training to agricultural cooperatives, and support environmental education programs in South Kivu Province.

projects.name: Nabahya Food Institute (NFI)
projects.excerpt:
NFI’s mission is to empower local agricultural cooperatives and reduce food insecurity in the DRC. Recognizing that food production is tied to environmental degradation, the organization is committed to addressing this dual challenge. NFI’s primary activities include regenerative agriculture, food security, clean energy, forest restoration initiatives, and investment in rural women.

The institute will use this grant to create sustainable forest reserves in villages within the territories of Uvira and Walungu, establish community nature clubs in target villages, and train local leaders in the target villages on the importance of sustainable tree planting and management.

projects.name: Advocates for Biodiversity Conservation
projects.excerpt:
Advocates for Biodiversity Conservation (ABC) is a non-profit organization based in Accra, Ghana, dedicated to biodiversity conservation and the mitigation of environmental degradation, with a strong emphasis on supporting sustainable livelihoods and empowering women in agriculture. With six years of experience, ABC has built partnerships with government agencies, private sector actors, communities, and civil society organizations to promote sustainable forest management, climate-smart practices, and landscape restoration. The organization integrates environmental conservation with social equity and economic development, and is recognized for its community engagement and capacity-building initiatives.

The proposed project aims to restore ecological function and enhance climate resilience across 1,250 hectares of degraded cocoa farmland in the Lower Bosomtwe area. The initiative will establish 120,000 native and multipurpose trees to improve canopy cover, soil fertility, and long-term farm productivity. ABC will empower smallholder farmers, youth, and women’s groups through training in nursery management, agroforestry, and sustainable livelihoods such as bamboo crafts and beekeeping. Restoration activities will be aligned with local and national development strategies, and community structures will be strengthened to ensure ongoing stewardship and maintenance. The project emphasizes participatory mapping, capacity building, and the integration of monitoring systems to support both environmental and socioeconomic outcomes.

projects.name: Agrointroductions Ghana (AIG)
projects.excerpt:
Agrointroductions Ghana (AIG) is a well-established non-profit environmental organization with a decade of experience advancing sustainable environmental practices in Ghana. Since 2014, AIG has focused on nature-based solutions, including reforestation, agroforestry, and agroecology, working in partnership with respected organizations such as the Green Climate Fund, UNDP GEF, and WWF. The organization is committed to empowering vulnerable communities, particularly in ecologically fragile areas, by promoting climate adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable livelihoods. AIG’s experienced team has successfully implemented projects that have improved local livelihoods and ecosystem resilience, with a strong emphasis on community engagement and innovative, scalable interventions.

The Reforest Plus Project aims to restore 350 hectares of degraded land in the Bosome-Freho area by planting 120,000 native trees through a combination of afforestation and agroforestry, while revitalizing biodiversity and supporting sustainable livelihoods for 1,000 direct beneficiaries, especially women and youth. The project will establish community-led restoration committees, set up a nursery for native seedlings, and engage local people in site preparation, planting, and ongoing maintenance. Smallholder farmers will receive training in climate-smart agriculture and agroecology, and will be supported to diversify their incomes through the integration of high-value tree crops. The initiative also includes targeted support for women and youth through alternative livelihood training and the creation of village savings and loans schemes, alongside capacity building for community-based forest governance. The project is designed to ensure community ownership, systematic implementation, and long-term sustainability, with regular monitoring and adaptive management to track ecological and socioeconomic outcomes.

projects.name: Ahadi Achievers Empowerment (AAE)
projects.excerpt:
In 2021, fifteen local development leaders from Kenya’s Makueni County came together to form AAE. Now, this community-based organization works with over 39 community self-help groups. Its mission is to empower and improve the quality of life of local communities through sustainable development initiatives, youth and women empowerment, and social inclusion.

With this grant, AAE will create five unique “village ecosystems” in Makueni, each comprising a diverse group of women, youths, and local decision makers. After a ten-day training program, these leaders will champion restoration in their communities by establishing tree nurseries and teaching others to care for the land.

projects.name: Climate Change Africa Opportunities (CCAO)
projects.excerpt:
Since 2015, CCAO has fought to protect biodiversity, promote socioeconomic development, and safeguard vulnerable ecosystems in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. CCAO employs a climate justice model, working especially with indigenous communities to build long-term climate resilience.

This second TerraFund grant will allow CCAO to expand its restoration work in the Rusizi Basin, bringing life back to an area that thousands of people rely on for food. The group will collaborate with indigenous committees to establish nurseries and monitor planting progress, putting them at the forefront of decision making.

projects.name: Fanteakwa District CCP Cooperative Cocoa Farmers and Marketing
projects.excerpt:
Formed in 2011, this cooperative is a Ghanaian non-profit organization that brings together 2,046 members from 25 societies. The group is devoted to working alongside local communities to promote cocoa farmers’ wellbeing, encourage youth to join the agribusiness sector, and enhance quality chocolate manufacturing.

With this grant, the union will work to incorporate native shade trees throughout cocoa farms in the districts of Fanteakwa, Atiwa, and Abuakwa. While the industry has historically led to degradation as farmers cleared the land for their crops, the new trees will revitalize the area and produce healthier, richer soil.

projects.name: Initiatives et Actions pour le Développement Local (IADL)
projects.excerpt:
IADL is a Congolese nonprofit working to improve food security and protect natural resources in the Kabare and Walungu Territories of South Kivu Province. To achieve this, IADL joins with grassroots partners and agricultural organizations to promote resilient, sustainable farming systems.

IADL will use this grant to expand its existing restoration efforts in Kabare Territory, a highly degraded mountainous region. In this area, where 80% of the population relies on agriculture for a living, the project will help to control soil erosion and tackle food insecurity.

projects.name: Nature and Development Foundation (NDF)
projects.excerpt:
Nature and Development Foundation (NDF) is a conservation organization with eight years of experience promoting responsible land use and biodiversity conservation through science-based field demonstrations and partnerships. With a mission to protect biodiversity while supporting local communities, NDF has established institutional credibility and has engaged in restoration activities, including collaborations with partners such as Emfed Farms on farm rehabilitation. The organization maintains strong relationships with the Forestry Commission and Community Resource Management Areas (CREMAs), leveraging these partnerships to implement projects that integrate sustainable timber production and restoration, despite being primarily based in Accra.

The proposed project aims to restore 128 hectares of degraded land in the Krokosu Forest Reserve using a mixed-species agroforestry approach (Modified Taungya System). The initiative will rebuild biodiversity, enhance carbon storage, and generate sustainable livelihoods for local communities through employment and apiculture. Approximately 500 community members will be engaged in site preparation, planting, and maintenance, with a focus on fair wages and gender equity. Training in forestry and beekeeping will build local capacity, while CREMAs will be supported to integrate apiculture as an additional income source. The project includes structured maintenance and monitoring, with regular community-led activities, supervisory visits, and oversight from the Forestry Commission to ensure high survival rates and ecosystem recovery. By embedding communities in management and benefit-sharing, the project will restore forest cover, improve soil and water retention, enhance biodiversity, and create new income streams, ultimately strengthening local stewardship and resilience to climate change.

projects.name: Initiative pour la Promotion de la Famille et du Genre (IPFG)
projects.excerpt:
Wezesha is a women-led nonprofit based in Kenya with five years of experience advancing climate resilience, ecosystem restoration, and sustainable livelihoods. The organization is dedicated to restoring degraded ecosystems, empowering women and youth, and strengthening community food security through regenerative agroforestry, reforestation, and climate-smart agriculture. Wezesha has built a strong reputation for engaging local communities in tree planting, sustainable land management, and the promotion of indigenous knowledge, equipping people with the skills and partnerships needed to protect their environment and livelihoods. Their community-anchored approach and demonstrated delivery capacity have established them as a credible and effective partner in restoration efforts, particularly in Nakuru County.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded landscapes and enhance biodiversity in and around Logoman and Bahati Forests through integrated forest restoration and agroforestry. Key activities include growing 50,000 trees in Logoman Forest to rehabilitate forest areas, establishing over 22,000 agroforestry and fruit trees on adjacent farms to improve food security and generate income, and installing 200 energy-efficient stoves in 100 nearby households to reduce wood fuel demand and protect young trees. The project will also train local trainers and farmers in soil and water conservation, engage community groups in all stages of restoration, and implement consistent tree maintenance and monitoring. Through these efforts, Wezesha expects to restore over 132 hectares of forest and farmland, strengthen ecosystem services and climate resilience, and improve local livelihoods by fostering sustainable land use, alternative income opportunities, and reduced pressure on natural forests.

projects.name: Obaatanpa Nyame Nti LTD
projects.excerpt:
Obaatanpa Nyame Nti Ltd (ONNL) is a Ghanaian company dedicated to sustainable forest restoration and community development. Founded in 2009 and led by a professional forester, ONNL has over 16 years of experience in establishing diverse forest plantations and providing consultancy services in forest management, wildfire control, nursery establishment, and community extension across several regions in Ghana. As a founding member of the Private Afforestation Developers’ Organization, ONNL has played a significant role in advancing restoration efforts both within and outside forest reserves. The company’s integrated approach, which includes a grocery branch to support financial sustainability, has created substantial employment opportunities for youth, women, and vulnerable groups in rural communities, reflecting its commitment to transparency, participation, and social inclusion.

The proposed project aims to restore 80 hectares of degraded land within the Bosomkese Forest Reserve through a community-driven approach that emphasizes biodiversity recovery, climate resilience, and improved livelihoods. ONNL will engage local stakeholders, including traditional leaders, women’s groups, and youth associations, to ensure inclusive participation and respect for local customs. The project will provide training and resources to farmers, promote agroforestry and beekeeping as alternative livelihoods, and create both permanent and casual jobs. Restoration activities will include nursery establishment, planting of indigenous species, regular maintenance, and fire management, supported by continuous monitoring and adaptive management. By integrating ecological restoration with social and economic benefits, the project seeks to build a resilient model that empowers local communities, enhances biodiversity, and supports long-term forest conservation in the Bosomkese area.

projects.name: Jeunesse Providence
projects.excerpt:
Jeunesse Providence, operating under the mission of AGAKURA, has three decades of experience empowering disadvantaged youth and their families through sustainable land use and agro-ecological practices. The organization is dedicated to building human, technical, and entrepreneurial capacities, with a strong focus on gender parity and youth engagement. Their expertise includes reforestation, soil erosion control, and biodiversity conservation, particularly through training and hands-on restoration activities such as establishing anti-erosion structures and maintaining woodlands. Over the years, they have made significant contributions to protecting degraded areas and agricultural lands, fostering both environmental and community resilience.

The proposed project targets the sub-hill of Giheta in Nyempundu, Mugina commune, aiming to promote sustainable land and resource management among approximately 200 households. The initiative will organize these households into a mixed association to manage watersheds and micro-woodlands, focusing on reforesting and protecting four small Ruhwa catchments and stabilizing riverbanks of three tributaries with bamboo planting. Activities include agroforestry interventions, such as planting trees and fruit species, establishing vegetated contour lines to reduce erosion, and providing training in agro-ecological practices to improve local livelihoods. The project also supports income-generating activities for women and youth, such as vegetable cultivation and fruit processing, while ensuring ongoing community engagement, monitoring, and adaptive management throughout the implementation period.

projects.name: Environment and Agroforestry Foundation (EAF)
projects.excerpt:
EAF is a non-profit organization devoted to natural resource management and biodiversity conservation in Ghana. The group boasts a wide range of activities, including land reclamation, farm technology improvement, and community education.
