Through this grant from TerraFund, EAF will restore the degraded farmlands and riparian forests along the Tain River in Ghana’s Bono Region. The project aims to improve local livelihoods, safeguard biodiversity, and promote agroforestry systems among local farmers. They encourage communities to plant cashew, African mahogany, and black afara trees for extra food and timber.

projects.name: Green Action Développement (GAD)
projects.excerpt: Originally founded to provide disaster relief, GAD now combines research with on-the-ground restoration techniques for a multifaceted approach to sustainable development. Based in the DRC’s South Kivu province, the non-profit organization takes international and locally recognized sustainable natural resource management techniques and advocates for them within the community. GAD will use this TerraFund grant to train farmers in Kalehe Territory, strengthening their knowledge in agroforestry techniques and providing a pathway to alternative livelihoods through beekeeping courses.

projects.name: Centre intervention et d’Action Communautaire (CIAC)
projects.excerpt:
Centre intervention et d’Action Communautaire (CIAC) is a national NGO based in Kigali, Rwanda, dedicated to empowering women and youth in rural farming communities. Since its establishment in 2021, CIAC has focused on advancing gender equality, sustainable agriculture, and environmental management through community-driven approaches. The organization is recognized for its use of the Plan Intégré du Paysan (PIP) model, which places women at the center of family-level planning and restoration efforts. CIAC’s experience includes leading agroforestry and climate resilience projects in partnership with local and international organizations, consistently promoting women’s leadership in restoration and livelihood improvement. Their transparent governance and strong track record in agroecology and community mobilization underpin their commitment to inclusive, sustainable development.

The proposed project targets the restoration of degraded landscapes in the Kivumu Sector, specifically Karambi cell in Rutsiro District, an area severely affected by erosion and poverty. CIAC aims to restore 260 hectares of land through women-led agroforestry, establishing two nurseries and planting 105,000 trees, with a focus on both native and exotic species. The initiative will form and train women’s and youth groups in nursery management, tree planting, and sustainable agriculture, while supporting 400 households in developing integrated agroforestry family plans. Demonstration plots, awareness campaigns, and peer-to-peer learning will foster community engagement and knowledge sharing. The project also integrates green enterprise development, including beekeeping, vermicomposting, and the creation of village savings and loan associations (VSLAs), to link income generation with landscape stewardship. A youth-led monitoring system using digital tools will ensure effective tracking of restoration progress, and performance-based incentives will encourage high tree survival rates. The project is expected to enhance biodiversity, create jobs, and improve livelihoods for both direct and indirect beneficiaries in the Karambi cell, aligning closely with local priorities for erosion control and socio-economic development.

projects.name: Wildlife Conservation Initiative (WCI)
projects.excerpt:
The Wildlife Conservation Initiative (WCI) is a Rwandan non-profit organization focused on ecosystem restoration, biodiversity conservation, and community empowerment. With four years of experience, WCI has established itself as a leader in community-led restoration, sustainable agriculture, and beekeeping, particularly engaging youth and women. The organization is recognized for its innovative approaches, such as integrating environmental education and agroecology, and for building strong partnerships with local and global stakeholders to ensure the sustainability and resilience of restored landscapes.

WCI proposes a project in the Kigeyo Sector, Rutsiro District, aimed at restoring degraded land along Lake Kivu buffer zones and hillsides by planting 105,000 indigenous and agroforestry trees. The initiative will organize local farmers into cooperatives, provide training in climate-smart cassava production, and support the cassava value chain to enhance livelihoods, especially for youth and women. A key innovation is the initiative to empower youth with digital skills for tree monitoring and environmental reporting, directly linking technology to restoration outcomes and new income opportunities. Activities include establishing a tree nursery, community engagement through sports, digital monitoring, and collaboration with local leaders to ensure long-term care and integration into district development plans. The project is expected to restore 160 hectares, protect riparian corridors, stabilize soils, and support over 2,000 households, while creating jobs and strengthening local cooperatives for improved market access.

projects.name: Forest of Hope Association (FHA)
projects.excerpt:
Established in Rwanda in 2012, FHA is a non-profit organization dedicated to advancing restoration across Rwanda’s Gishwati Forest, which has lost nearly all of its tree cover. The group engages local communities in restoring protected areas, improving livelihoods and reducing human-wildlife conflicts, all with the goal of turning the Gishwati Forest into a National Park.

With this grant from TerraFund, FHA will implement a new project in the area designed to empower local residents, provide training on seedling production and tree growing, and build resilience to climate change through intensive restoration.

projects.name: Seed Savers Network Association (SSN-K)
projects.excerpt:
Seed Savers Network Association (SSN-K) is a national grassroots organization in Kenya, established in 2009, dedicated to conserving agrobiodiversity and strengthening community seed systems to enhance food sovereignty. With 15 years of experience, SSN-K has engaged over 405,000 community members and leads Africa’s largest network of community seedbanks. The organization operates an agroecology learning center and an incubation hub for value addition, and has restored more than 2,500 hectares of degraded land through agroecological approaches. SSN-K is recognized for its innovative integration of restoration, agroecology, and seed systems, effectively linking ecological outcomes with improved community livelihoods.

The proposed project will intensify environmental restoration and promote land degradation neutrality in Mau, Mauche, and Likia areas of Nakuru County, aiming to enhance climate resilience and local livelihoods. The initiative will restore 120 hectares of degraded land by planting 100,000 trees—including a mix of indigenous, fruit, and nitrogen-fixing species—while supporting community nurseries and farmer-led training. It will also conserve 12 kilometers of riverline to improve water services, introduce soil conservation measures, and supply planting materials to riverside communities. Agroecological practices will be integrated through farmer-to-farmer training, establishment of community seedbanks, and support for women and youth enterprise incubation. The project prioritizes youth and women, aiming to improve environmental management, create jobs, enhance food security, and conserve local tree seeds, with regular monitoring and community involvement to ensure sustained impact.

projects.name: Europe Autoland Limited
projects.excerpt:
Europe Autoland Limited is dedicated to restoring degraded land through sustainable agro-forestry, with nearly three decades of experience in the field. The organization focuses on cultivating teak, mango, cocoa, and staple crops in integrated systems that conserve soil, capture carbon, and support rural livelihoods. Their mission emphasizes climate-smart farming, large-scale tree planting, and community engagement, particularly empowering youth and women. Over the years, they have built a strong track record in landscape restoration, job creation, and climate resilience by working closely with local communities and investing in sustainable practices.

The proposed project seeks to restore degraded land and expand forest cover in the Europa Forest Reserve in Derma, Tano-South District of the Ahafo Region through a large-scale afforestation initiative. The plan involves planting 85,000 trees across 100 hectares, using a mix of teak, mahogany, and indigenous species. Local communities, especially women, youth, and smallholder farmers, will be actively involved in all stages, from land preparation and nursery management to planting and long-term care, ensuring sustainable benefits and alternative livelihoods. The project includes comprehensive maintenance for at least three years, with regular watering, mulching, firebreaks, and pest management, supported by a dedicated monitoring team using both physical inspections and digital mapping. The initiative aims to restore ecosystem health, sequester significant amounts of carbon, create local jobs, and strengthen community resilience and biodiversity.

projects.name: FDINDA
projects.excerpt:
FDINDA is a diversified Rwandan company with a decade of experience in sustainable macadamia farming, organic fertilizer production, livestock rearing, and animal feed. Committed to ethical and environmentally responsible practices, FDINDA supports local growers by distributing macadamia seedlings and purchasing harvested nuts, which are processed for local sale. The organization has established itself as a leader in the sector, integrating innovation and sustainability to empower communities, create employment, and promote premium quality nut production. Its track record includes significant engagement with smallholder farmers and a strong focus on community enrichment and environmental stewardship.

The proposed Green Growth & Community Empowerment Initiative in Karongi aims to advance climate-smart agriculture, value addition, and community resilience. FDINDA will establish a modern tree nursery to produce 90,000 macadamia and agroforestry seedlings, planting a portion on its own land and distributing the rest to smallholder farmers to restore 430 hectares. The project includes setting up a macadamia processing facility to convert nuts-in-shell into export-ready kernels, diversifying income for over 1,000 farmers. Livelihoods will be further enhanced through apiculture, empowering at least 100 households—especially women and youth—by integrating beekeeping for pollination and honey production. Training sessions will build local capacity in nursery management, climate-smart practices, and apiculture, while organic fertilizer production will improve soil health. The initiative is designed to sequester carbon, support Rwanda’s climate goals, and foster a resilient agroforestry ecosystem, positioning FDINDA as a catalyst for sustainable, inclusive growth in the Karongi region.

projects.name: Excelsa Forestry Renewables Ghana Limited
projects.excerpt:
Excelsa will implement a large-scale restoration program covering 171 hectares in priority landscapes. This effort will involve the planting of 90,000 economic and indigenous trees. Excelsa will restore 171 hectares through agroforestry plantation development, planting 9 native and high-value timber species to enhance biodiversity corridors and support sustainable wood value chains. Urban and riparian greening initiatives will be done through contract services for cooperatives and NGOs.

Beyond tree planting, Excelsa’s model emphasizes farmer training, community engagement, and long-term maintenance to ensure high survival rates and lasting impact. By integrating restoration with livelihood opportunities, we aim to build resilient rural economies, sequester significant amounts of carbon, and contribute to Ghana’s national targets for climate change mitigation and forest cover recovery. Through this project, Excelsa is demonstrating that nature-based solutions can simultaneously deliver economic returns, ecological regeneration, and climate benefits when designed with farmers and local communities.

projects.name: Community Organization for Positive Impact, Care & Development (COPICAD)
projects.excerpt:
Since 2017, COPICAD has engaged in environmental conservation, land restoration and social-economic empowerment of youth, women and the most vulnerable in the community.

This funding will equip COPICAD to regreen the forests around the degraded Lake Olbolosat, ensuring a sustainable water supply for millions of people in the county. This work will also protect the rich biodiversity of the river basin, home to its well-known hippos and over 300 species of birds.

projects.name: Jumuisha Initiative
projects.excerpt:
Jumuisha Initiative unites youth and women for education, support, and social change in Kenya’s Makueni County. The organization’s environmental protection unit works in tandem with the local government to accelerate regreening.

It will use this grant to help native species flourish, restore biodiversity, and promote overall ecosystem resilience in Makueni County’s Kibwezi East constituency. The project aims to transform agriculture and improve farmers’ food security by dotting their cropland with fruit trees.

projects.name: Kimplanter Seedlings and Nurseries Ltd
projects.excerpt:
Kimplanter is a Kenyan commercial propagation company that supplies drought-resistant seedlings for vegetables and fruit, indigenous and exotic tree species. Its mission is to promote land restoration, improve climate mitigation and food production, and empower local famers in semi-arid regions.

This investment will mitigate soil depletion, flash floods and the gully formations characteristic of semi-arid areas. The company will engage with landowners and public institutions in Kajiado County, Kenya to promote reforestation and fruit tree planting.

projects.name: Kukuom Cooperative Cocoa Farmers and Marketing Union
projects.excerpt:
Kukuom Union is an organized cooperative for cocoa-growing families in Ghana. It first began with few farmers who volunteered to help each other with activities like weeding, harvesting, and breaking down cocoa pods. The cooperative was officially established in 2011 and since then has rapidly expanded, now supporting 3,601 members across 29 communities.

Kukuom Union will use this grant to rehabilitate old cocoa fields, integrate trees into existing farms, and establish new cultivation areas across the cooperative. The project will embrace assisted natural regeneration techniques, using just a touch of human intervention to give trees on cocoa farms the space that they need to grow.

projects.name: Resource Conservation Initiative (RESCONI)
projects.excerpt:
RESCONI aims to protect the livelihoods of forest fringe communities in Ghana, training them on sustainable natural resource management and securing a voice for them in decision-making processes. It also advocates for community education and promotes research on natural resource extraction and conservation.

RESCONI will use this grant to renew the degraded lands of the Asutifi North District and the Atwima Mponua District. Community members will grow trees along habitat corridors, attracting birds, insects, and other wildlife to restore ecological balance.

projects.name: Save Kenya Water Towers
projects.excerpt:
Recognizing the crucial role of engaging youth in forest restoration, Save Kenya Water Towers purchases and distributes seedlings to schools and institutions. Over the last ten years, the organization has grown more than 10 million trees and rehabilitated several catchment areas in the Cherangani Water Towers, Mount Elgon and Mau Forest. It has also partnered with the Kenya Forest Service and other environmental institutions to set up tree nurseries.

Save Kenya Water Towers will use this grant to cultivate diverse tree species and rehabilitate parts of the Greater Rift Valley that have been degraded by unsustainable agricultural practices.

projects.name: Shamba Ndogo Miti Mingi CBO
projects.excerpt:
Shamba Ndogo Miti Mingi CBO is a community-based organization rooted in the Mau Forest region, with over a decade of experience in land restoration and community empowerment. Originating as a self-help group in 2014 and formalized as a CBO in 2021, the organization is inclusive, involving people living with disabilities in leadership roles. Their mission centers on restoring degraded lands by producing affordable, high-quality indigenous tree species, conserving biodiversity, and promoting sustainable ecosystems. They have established a self-sustaining model that combines income-generating activities with grants, providing seedlings, technical support, and capacity-building to local communities. Their track record includes significant contributions to restoration, biodiversity conservation, and community resilience, underpinned by a strong business approach and a revenue-generating nursery.

The proposed project aims to restore approximately 60 hectares of degraded land around the Mau Forest, particularly in the Logman Forest area and adjacent farmlands. The initiative will establish over 75,000 trees, blending indigenous and agroforestry species to enhance biodiversity, stabilize soils, and strengthen ecosystem resilience. Local residents, especially women, youth, and smallholder farmers, will be engaged in nursery management, tree planting, and aftercare, creating over 40 jobs and fostering community ownership. The project will also introduce two modern apiaries to support honey production and pollination, benefiting 300 households, and distribute 7,500 avocado seedlings to 750 farmers to promote sustainable agroforestry income. Comprehensive training sessions will build community capacity in nursery management, sustainable land use, aquaculture, and beekeeping. Maintenance and monitoring will be ongoing, with regular community-led activities to ensure high tree survival rates and long-term impact, ultimately improving the livelihoods of at least 2,000 households and contributing to the environmental and social resilience of the Mau Forest region.

projects.name: Sprouted Roots LBG
projects.excerpt:
Sprouted Roots LBG is dedicated to strengthening cooperative systems and supporting ethical sourcing to build resilient agricultural communities. With five years of experience, the organization works closely with farmers and cooperatives to enhance productivity and sustainability through capacity building, certification, and agroforestry practices. Their mission emphasizes empowering women and youth, promoting environmentally responsible practices, and linking producers to premium markets. Sprouted Roots LBG has engaged in innovative agricultural value chain initiatives, aiming to ensure that farming communities thrive both socially and economically while contributing to global sustainable sourcing.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded cocoa landscapes in Bosome Freho and Bosumtwe by establishing resilient agroforestry systems. The initiative will focus on restoring 2,000 hectares using climate-resilient native species and planting 80,000 trees across cocoa farms in Kokotro, Yapasaa, Kokobeng, Minti, Brodekwano, Abuontem, and Asamama. Activities include community engagement, farmer training, land preparation, planting cycles, and ongoing maintenance such as weeding, fire management, and survival assessments. The project will also train and equip youth in cocoa value chain services, introduce fine-flavor cocoa and alternative livelihoods, and strengthen cooperatives to improve market access and income diversification for 1,000 smallholder farmers. The approach integrates sustainable land management, environmental stewardship, and capacity building to enhance biodiversity, climate resilience, and community livelihoods.

projects.name: Vokenel Enterprises Limited
projects.excerpt:
Vokenel Enterprises Limited is a Kenyan social enterprise established in 2017, specializing in the processing of baobab fruit powder and baobab oil. With eight years of experience, the organization has built a robust value chain by sourcing baobab fruits from over a thousand farmers in Makueni County, a semi-arid region. Vokenel is committed to sustainable practices, operating a seedling nursery for drought-resistant tree species such as baobab, tamarind, acacia, and melia volkensii. The organization partners closely with local communities in Kibwezi East and West to restore degraded land through tree planting, demonstrating a strong track record in both environmental restoration and community engagement.

The proposed project aims to drive business growth and enhance land restoration efforts in Makueni County. Vokenel will develop a new baobab husk planting medium from production waste, promoting circularity and providing a sustainable alternative for nurseries and hydroponic farming. Funding will support the acquisition of processing equipment, expansion of baobab oil production, and attainment of international food safety certification to access broader markets. The project will also strengthen local supply chains by purchasing more baobab fruits from farmers and investing in the expansion of community nurseries. In partnership with the Kibwezi Forest Fighters Community Based Organization, Vokenel plans to plant 80,000 trees across farmlands, schools, dispensaries, and churches, while supporting nursery protection through the installation of beehives to deter elephants. The initiative integrates community mobilization, nursery management, and ongoing tree maintenance to ensure high survival rates and lasting environmental impact.

projects.name: Friends of Environment and Social Development (FESD)
projects.excerpt:
FESD is a Rwandan non-profit organization that was established in 2018 by 33 local environmental activists. It equips communities to be at the forefront of forest restoration and environmental conservation through tree planting, restoration projects, and agricultural training.

With a TerraFund grant, FESD aims to restore the degraded lands of Rwanda’s Nzahaha Sector. While it plans to work with all residents, the organization will focus on women-led households, training them to establish community sapling nurseries and personal kitchen gardens.

projects.name: Lake Ol'bolossat Community Conservation Group (LOCCOG)
projects.excerpt:
LOCCOG was established as a Kenyan environmental non-profit organization in 2019. It champions the environmental conservation of Lake Ol'Bolossat and its surrounding area, all while preserving vital ecological functions and involving a wide range of stakeholders. The group has brought together more than 45 community conservation groups with more than 5,000 members to partner on restoration projects.

LOCCOG will use this grant to restore degraded forests, riparian zones, and farms throughout Nyandura County. These renewed landscapes will ward off landslides and rock falls, protecting nearby residents from harm.

projects.name: Mouvement pour Christ au Rwanda (MPCR)
projects.excerpt:
Mouvement pour Christ au Rwanda (MPCR) is a faith-based NGO with 15 years of experience in holistic community development, focusing on empowering vulnerable populations through spiritual transformation, environmental restoration, sustainable agriculture, and youth empowerment. The organization has a strong track record in implementing projects that build community capacity, foster partnerships, and promote long-term resilience and well-being. MPCR is recognized for its community engagement and expertise in environmental conservation, with notable achievements in sustainable agriculture and socio-economic resilience initiatives.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded farmland in Rwanda’s Western Province, Rutsiro District, specifically in Boneza Sector, Nkira Cell, Gisiza and Gisoro Villages, by adopting climate-resilient agroforestry systems. The initiative will plant 75,000 trees—including exotic, indigenous, and fruit species—across 250 hectares, integrating them into existing farming systems to enhance biodiversity, food security, and ecosystem health. Activities include community mobilization, nursery establishment, tree planting, and ongoing maintenance, supported by five farmer groups and Community Vigilance Committees. The project also promotes diversified livelihoods through kitchen gardens and savings groups, creates inclusive job opportunities, and builds local capacity in sustainable land management. Continuous monitoring, community-based oversight, and knowledge sharing are embedded to ensure sustainability and integration with local development plans.

projects.name: Woman Development Initiative (WDI)
projects.excerpt:
WDI promotes women’s socioeconomic development and environmental protection in Burundi. It mobilizes local agro-pastoral groups, local ministries and government agencies, and international organizations to conserve and restore forests and help communities adapt to the effects of climate change.

WDI will use its TerraFund grant to provide rural households with seedlings that will transform into wood-producing, fruit-bearing, and crop-protecting trees. This will enhance food security and improve community incomes, building on their decades of work. This project takes place in Commune Mubimbi of Bujumbura Province

projects.name: Wezesha
projects.excerpt:
Wezesha is a women-led nonprofit based in Kenya with five years of experience advancing climate resilience, ecosystem restoration, and sustainable livelihoods. The organization is dedicated to restoring degraded ecosystems, empowering women and youth, and strengthening community food security through regenerative agroforestry, reforestation, and climate-smart agriculture. Wezesha has built a strong reputation for engaging local communities in tree planting, sustainable land management, and the promotion of indigenous knowledge, equipping people with the skills and partnerships needed to protect their environment and livelihoods. Their community-anchored approach and demonstrated delivery capacity have established them as a credible and effective partner in restoration efforts, particularly in Nakuru County.

The proposed project aims to restore degraded landscapes and enhance biodiversity in and around Logoman and Bahati Forests through integrated forest restoration and agroforestry. Key activities include growing 50,000 trees in Logoman Forest to rehabilitate forest areas, establishing over 22,000 agroforestry and fruit trees on adjacent farms to improve food security and generate income, and installing 200 energy-efficient stoves in 100 nearby households to reduce wood fuel demand and protect young trees. The project will also train local trainers and farmers in soil and water conservation, engage community groups in all stages of restoration, and implement consistent tree maintenance and monitoring. Through these efforts, Wezesha expects to restore over 132 hectares of forest and farmland, strengthen ecosystem services and climate resilience, and improve local livelihoods by fostering sustainable land use, alternative income opportunities, and reduced pressure on natural forests.

projects.name: Centre for Sustainability and Environmental Action (CSEA)
projects.excerpt:
The Centre for Sustainability and Environmental Action (CSEA) is dedicated to promoting environmental sustainability, women and youth empowerment, effective governance, and the protection and management of natural resources. With five years of experience, CSEA has established itself as a leader in community-driven restoration, leveraging research, advocacy, coalition building, and education to advance climate action and inclusiveness. The organization is recognized for its participatory approach, engaging local communities and stakeholders to foster healthier and more just societies, and has contributed to ecological restoration through initiatives that integrate local knowledge and prioritize gender inclusion.

CSEA proposes to restore 120 hectares of degraded forest landscapes in the Bosome-Freho District by implementing community-led agroforestry and alternative livelihood strategies. The project will integrate timber, fruit, and staple tree species to enhance biodiversity, improve soil and water health, and strengthen climate resilience, while also supporting local livelihoods and food security. Activities include planting over 70,000 seedlings across four communities, establishing community nurseries, training at least 500 community members—especially women and youth—in restoration and alternative income activities, and forming local governance structures to ensure long-term stewardship. The project emphasizes participatory planning, ongoing community engagement, and robust monitoring using both traditional and technological methods. Expected outcomes include improved ecosystem health, increased biodiversity, enhanced rural livelihoods, and contributions to national and global climate goals, with a strong focus on sustainability and community ownership.

projects.name: Vert Limited
projects.excerpt:
Vert Limited is a Kenyan agro-processing company established in 2006, known for its leadership in cultivating, processing, and exporting high-quality agricultural products such as dried fruits, fruit purees, and fresh produce. With nearly two decades of experience, Vert partners with over 5,000 smallholder farmers, focusing on empowering rural communities, especially women and youth, through sustainable farming and value addition. The company is recognized for its innovative mango processing and strong commitment to social impact, quality, and community development.

The proposed project aims to restore dryland farms in Makueni County by planting 70,000 new mango trees in collaboration with smallholder farmers, particularly in high-yielding areas like Makueni, Mbooni, and Kibwezi West. Vert will work with certified nurseries and agricultural partners to provide clean planting stock, deliver targeted farmer training, and support the formation of farmer groups for efficient input supply and market access. The project integrates digital tree tagging and monitoring to ensure traceability and compliance, while technical support and regular extension visits will help farmers adopt best practices. By increasing mango coverage, the initiative seeks to boost family incomes, enhance climate resilience, reduce post-harvest losses, and strengthen Vert’s value chain, ultimately delivering significant economic and environmental benefits to the region.

projects.name: Greening Burundi
projects.excerpt:
Greening Burundi is a youth-led non-profit organization that promotes climate resilience initiatives in schools and communities across the provinces of Cibitoke and Bubanza. The organization’s vision centers around preserving and growing Burundi’s forests, eradicating poverty, and bolstering food security.

Greening Burundi will use this grant to expand its current restoration activities in Kibira National Park at the center of the Albertine Rift. This lush landscape is known not only for supplying water to Central and East Africa, but also for being home to a great number of endangered species like Grauer’s broadbill and the chimpanzee.

projects.name: Association of Women in Agriculture Kenya (AWAK)
projects.excerpt:
The Association of Women in Agriculture Kenya (AWAK) is a women-led, non-profit organization dedicated to advancing ecosystem restoration, climate justice, and resilient livelihoods through a gender-centered approach. With eight years of experience, AWAK empowers women and youth as leaders in climate action, focusing on agroforestry and food forests to restore degraded landscapes and improve food security. The organization is recognized for its community-led restoration initiatives, integrating sustainable agriculture, clean energy, and livelihood diversification. AWAK’s commitment to gender inclusion and ecological balance has established it as a credible leader in gender-responsive restoration and agroforestry in Kenya.

AWAK proposes a six-year project in Bahati (Bavuni area, Nakuru County) to restore degraded farmland through community-led agroforestry and food forests. The project aims to plant 60,000 trees, benefiting 600 smallholder farmers, with women and youth leading restoration efforts. Activities include establishing farmer-managed agroforestry plots, food forests, and woodlots, alongside training 24 Green Women and Youth Champions to lead farmer training and aftercare. The project emphasizes participatory planning, capacity building in agroecology, and strong community engagement to ensure long-term stewardship. By integrating soil and water conservation, livelihood co-benefits, and market linkages, the initiative seeks to improve nutrition, food security, and climate resilience in Bavuni, while building a replicable, gender-responsive restoration model.

projects.name: Saving and Conservation of Our Planet Earth Intervention (SCOPE Intervention)
projects.excerpt:
Scope Intervention (Saving and Conservation of Our Planet Earth Intervention) is a non-profit organization working to initiate and promote local initiatives that contribute to the global fight against climate change. The organization’s climate change adaptation and mitigation actions contribute to environmental conservation while enhancing local communities’ climate change coping mechanisms. The organization is also working to promote respect on human rights and stimulate socio-economic activities that contribute to poverty reduction.

The organization has been active in the restoration of Torok River and Kaptagat in Elgeyo Marakwet County; Mau Forest Complex and Water Towers among other ecosystems in Kenya.

projects.name: Slow Food Convivia Association of Kenya (Slow Food Kenya)
projects.excerpt:
Established in 2014, Slow Food Conviva Association of Kenya is an affiliate of Slow Food International, a global organization whose mission is to prevent the disappearance of local food cultures and traditions. The organization works with farmers to encourage them to grow climate resilient crops and trees.

Slow Food Convivia will use the grant to champion a women and youth-led climate initiative to restore the Mau Forest ecosystem. It will secure incomes for these groups by training them to grow fruit, make sawdust briquettes, and run tree seedling nurseries.

projects.name: Consortium: J & R Engineering and General Business; GreenGoal Rwanda
projects.excerpt:
J&R Engineering is a company that offers a range of tailored environmental services to address the pressing challenges of land degradation, soil erosion, and habitat destruction. It is partnering with GreenGoal Rwanda, a local social enterprise that offers accessible and affordable native tree seedlings to farmers.

This investment will support the companies’ efforts to increase seedling production and nursery management, increase tree survival rates when they are planted across farms, and boost sources of sustainable income for youth and women. The consortium’s goal will restore ecosystem services and biodiversity in Rwanda’s Rusizi and Nyamasheke districts while improving livelihoods.

projects.name: Grow Tech Nurseries
projects.excerpt:
Grow Tech Nurseries is an agricultural and forest biotechnology company based in Nakuru, Kenya. It specializes in mass propagation of various trees for forest restoration, such as croton, lemon verbena, paulownia, sandalwood, and other species that are native to the Mau Forest. The company also propagates crops through tissue culture, including several varieties of bananas and bamboo.

An investment from TerraFund will bolster Grow Tech’s efforts to restore the rapidly dwindling Eastern Mau Forest by working with partners to supply native trees and bamboo species that provide sustainable revenue to local communities. The company will also expand the tissue culture laboratory that makes its tree propagation possible.

projects.name: Perfect Village Communities (PVC Burundi)
projects.excerpt:
PVC is a Burundian social enterprise that works both within the country and across East Africa. Its approaches are rooted in regenerative agricultural practices and aim to improve the livelihoods of rural farming communities. The business restores land, sells value-added wood products, and enhances farmers’ access to health services.

With an investment from TerraFund, Perfect Village Communities plans to create jobs primarily for women and youths, grow revenue-generating trees, and lead training and awareness raising programs in the provinces of Bujumbura, Bubanza, and Cibitoke.

projects.name: Talmond
projects.excerpt:
Talmond is a women-led Ghanaian company bringing the world's first tropical almond and fonio milk to the home and global market. As the first pioneer of the new tropical almond agroforestry industry in Ghana, the company uses climate- and water-resilient crops to promote biodiversity.

An investment from TerraFund will help Talmond bring its product to market, attract more investors, and scale its business across the globe.

projects.name: Habelle's Foundation
projects.excerpt:
Habelle’s Foundation is committed to restoring degraded ecosystems and improving community wellbeing through inclusive, community-driven approaches. With three years of experience, the organization focuses on practical restoration methods that blend scientific and indigenous knowledge, working closely with women, youth, farmers, and local institutions. Their initiatives span tree planting, sustainable land management, and green livelihood development, aiming to rebuild biodiversity, protect water sources, and create lasting economic opportunities. Habelle’s Foundation emphasizes partnership, local ownership, and measurable impact, ensuring that restoration efforts lead to resilient landscapes and stronger communities.

The proposed project seeks to restore 30 hectares of degraded forest-reserve land in the Juaboso–Bia area by planting 38,000 climate-resilient trees and integrating nature-based livelihoods such as mushroom cultivation and beekeeping. The initiative will engage and train local women and youth, create direct employment, and benefit around 200 community members. Activities include establishing nurseries, conducting capacity-building sessions, planting and maintaining trees, and launching livelihood enterprises. The project also involves community sensitization on sustainable land use and climate adaptation, with ongoing monitoring and stewardship to ensure long-term ecological recovery, improved soil and watershed health, and sustainable management of restored forest lands.

projects.name: Rights and Advocacy Initiatives Network (RAIN)
projects.excerpt:
Rights and Advocacy Initiatives Network (RAIN) is a Ghanaian non-governmental organization established in 2019, dedicated to fostering a resilient environment through rights-based approaches in agriculture, natural resources, and environmental sectors. With a focus on community rights, inclusive forest governance, climate-smart agriculture, and gender empowerment, RAIN has built a reputation for effective advocacy, capacity development, and policy interventions. The organization is recognized for its strong local partnerships, particularly with the Forest Services Division, and its commitment to community-driven restoration and sustainable livelihoods.

The proposed project aims to empower farmers in two forest fringe communities near the Fum Headwaters Forest Reserve in the Bosome Freho District by integrating forest restoration with sustainable livelihood development. Through climate awareness campaigns, reforestation of 32 hectares using the Modified Taungya System and agroforestry, and prioritization of indigenous species, the project seeks to enhance biodiversity, sequester carbon, and improve economic opportunities. Activities include stakeholder engagement, capacity building in nursery establishment and tree management, support for agroforestry and apiculture, and formalization of benefit-sharing arrangements. Continuous monitoring, knowledge sharing, and inclusive participation of women, youth, and migrants are central to ensuring the long-term sustainability and community ownership of the restoration efforts.

projects.name: Endao Water Resource Users Association (Endao WRUA)
projects.excerpt:
EWRUA is a community-led non-profit organization in Kenya’s Baringo County. Dedicated to protecting local water resources, the group grows trees to enhance catchment restoration, builds gabions, and installs water harvesting tanks to ensure a steady water supply for all. EWRUA works diligently to provide opportunities for community members to engage firsthand in environmental conservation.

This funding will allow EWRUA to restore the Kirandich Dam catchment area and the five streams that feed into it. The trees that they plant will filter pollutants from the dam and prevent runoff, providing cleaner water for nearby residents.

projects.name: Bright Generation Community Foundation
projects.excerpt:
Bright Generation Community Foundation (BGCF) is a Ghanaian non-profit dedicated to restoring degraded landscapes and building climate resilience through community empowerment. With three years of experience, BGCF specializes in cultivating bamboo and indigenous trees, engaging women and youth in nursery management, and promoting sustainable bamboo value chains. The organization has established strong partnerships with traditional leaders, schools, and local authorities, and is recognized for its commitment to ecological restoration and socio-economic development in local communities.

The Bosomtwe Forest Restoration Project seeks to restore 35 hectares of degraded forest reserve in the Bosomtwe District by planting 38,000 mixed tree species, improving soil protection, and stabilizing watersheds. The project integrates a bamboo-based livelihood component, including the establishment of a bamboo greenhouse to supply seedlings for both restoration and community income generation. Activities include community mobilization, nursery establishment, training in silviculture and fire management, phased planting, agroforestry demonstration plots, and ongoing ecological monitoring. The initiative emphasizes community leadership, particularly involving women and youth, and aims to create sustainable green livelihoods, enhance biodiversity, reduce erosion, and foster long-term stewardship of restored lands through structured governance and strong local engagement.

projects.name: PROMACNUTS LTD
projects.excerpt:
PROMACNUTS LTD is dedicated to restoring degraded land and promoting sustainable economic development through macadamia-based agroforestry. With 15 years of experience, the organization has built expertise in producing and distributing high-quality grafted macadamia seedlings, training communities in tree cultivation, and supporting farmers with technical guidance. Their mission centers on empowering farmers with income-generating crops, enhancing biodiversity, and fostering climate resilience. PROMACNUTS has a strong track record in community development, value chain integration, and establishing partnerships that optimize benefits for smallholder farmers.

The proposed project aims to restore 85 hectares of degraded land by planting over 54,000 macadamia and agroforestry trees, supporting farmers in site preparation, planting, and maintenance, and integrating soil conservation practices. The initiative will provide training in climate-smart agriculture and macadamia production, targeting equitable participation of women and youth. PROMACNUTS will facilitate collective marketing, establish savings groups to strengthen financial inclusion, and create jobs through the development of a robust macadamia value chain. The project is designed to improve household incomes, enhance food security through intercropping, and ensure long-term sustainability by building local capacity and linking farmers to markets and microfinance institutions.

projects.name: Ngeli Ventures Limited "Ngeli Foods"
projects.excerpt:
Ngeli Ventures Limited, operating as Ngeli Foods, is an innovative organic food company in Kenya with a strong focus on apiculture conservation and the production of high-quality bee products. Over the past four years, the organization has established itself as a leader in integrating sustainable agriculture with environmental restoration, particularly through its work with smallholder farmers. Ngeli Foods is recognized for its commitment to empowering local communities, especially women and youth, by promoting agroecological practices that enhance both livelihoods and ecosystem health.

The proposed project aims to restore up to 80 acres of degraded farmland in Kilungu, Makueni, by planting 25,000 climate-resilient and indigenous trees over three years. The initiative will improve soil fertility, boost biodiversity, and reduce land conversion pressures by training 300 smallholder farmers—half of whom are women and youth—in climate-smart farming, agroforestry, and sustainable beekeeping. A tree-linked incentive scheme will reward farmers who maintain multipurpose trees with premium honey prices, while community restoration committees will oversee tree care and protection. The project will also establish nurseries, apiaries, and a digital monitoring system to track progress, ensuring high tree survival rates and linking restoration efforts to increased household incomes and enhanced pollination. Through continuous mentorship, digital traceability, and market linkages, the project seeks to create lasting environmental and economic benefits for the region.

projects.name: Justdiggit
projects.excerpt:
Justdiggit’s mission is to make dry land green again by inspiring and activating farmers in Africa. In Kenya, the group’s regreening projects are in the South Rift, a region that is home to 240,000 Maasai pastoralists and some of the richest mammal diversity in the world.

Through this second TerraFund grant, Justdiggit will extend its existing partnership with SORALO to grow nearly 50000 trees in the South Rift. The project will work with this local pastoralist organization to naturally regenerate the landscape.

projects.name: Afarinick Company Limited
projects.excerpt: Afarinick Company Limited, a leader in climate-smart agriculture and sustainable land-use systems, proposes to support smallholder cocoa farmers establish 100 hectares of cocoa agroforestry farms in the Volta Region of Ghana. This initiative aligns with national goals for reforestation, youth employment, and climate resilience, while creating inclusive economic opportunities for local communities. Project objectives are as follows • Establish 100 hectares of cocoa agroforestry farms integrating cocoa and high-value tree species (e.g., mahogany, Albizia sp, fruit trees). • Create sustainable employment for over 300 women and youth in surrounding communities. • Enhance biodiversity and carbon sequestration in degraded landscapes through agroforestry practices. • Build local capacity in agroforestry techniques, nursery management practices and additional livelihood projects. Afarinick will adopt a participatory approach to ensure local ownership and long-term success. Community durbars shall be organized to introduce the project and its benefits; adopt inclusive recruitment and training, prioritizing women and youth roles in nursery management, tree planting and maintenance; and providing hands-on training in agroforestry and climate-smart practices. Using the registered and trained labour force (Rehab Assistants) from the communities, selected farms shall be cleared, lined and pegged, established with improved cocoa seedling varieties and local economic shade trees (including plantain to serve as additional livelihood to farmers) and maintained over the project period to ensure survival. To install cocoa agroforestry on 100 hectares will require 110,000 cocoa seedlings, 9,000 economic tree seedlings and 105,600 plantain seedlings. Planting economic shade trees along with plantain on cocoa farms provide microclimate conducive for cocoa plants to thrive. The planting of 105,600 plantain seedlings provides temporary shade for the planted cocoa seedlings. Additionally, plantain serves as additional livelihoods for farmers.

stories.title: How One Woman is Leading the Restoration of 10,000 Hectares in Tanzania
stories.excerpt: Amina Njau started with three seedlings and a dream. Today her cooperative employs 340 women and has restored a watershed sustaining five villages in the Kilosa district.
body: When Amina Njau planted her first three tree seedlings behind her home in Kilosa district in 2016, she had no way of knowing it would grow into one of Tanzania's largest women-led restoration cooperatives.

Eight years later, the Kilosa Women's Restoration Cooperative that Amina founded employs 340 women across five villages, running tree nurseries, managing a 10,000-hectare watershed restoration area, and training neighbouring communities in agroforestry techniques.
"We started because our rivers were drying up and our children were walking further every year for water," Amina says. "Now those same rivers run again in the dry season."

VIA Foundation began supporting the cooperative in 2021 with a technical assistance grant, followed by multi-year flexible funding that allowed Amina's team to purchase nursery equipment and formalise land-tenure agreements with local government — a critical step that secured the cooperative's long-term access to the land it restores.

stories.title: Satellite Technology Transforms How Africa Measures Restoration
stories.excerpt: VIA Foundation's monitoring framework combines satellite imagery with community data.
body: For years, verifying restoration outcomes across remote African landscapes meant costly, infrequent field visits — leaving long gaps where degradation or project failure could go unnoticed.

VIA Foundation's monitoring and verification team has built a framework that layers satellite imagery, machine-learning canopy analysis, and community-reported field data into a single dashboard updated monthly across all active project sites.

The system flags underperforming plots automatically, letting field teams intervene early rather than discovering a failed planting a year later — and gives funders real-time, independently verifiable confidence in reported outcomes.

stories.title: Blended Finance Model Unlocks $12M for Sahel Restoration
stories.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind financial structure de-risks investment in dryland ecosystems.
body: Dryland restoration has historically struggled to attract commercial capital — returns are slow, and the ecological risk profile is unfamiliar to most investors.

VIA Foundation's new blended finance facility pairs a philanthropic first-loss layer with co-investment from regional development banks, absorbing early risk so private capital can enter with confidence.
The structure has mobilised $12M for dryland restoration projects across the Sahel in its first year, a model VIA Foundation now plans to replicate for coastal and highland landscapes.

stories.title: Training 5,000 Youth as Africa's Next Generation of Restoration Leaders
stories.excerpt: A pan-African training program builds ecological expertise and creates green jobs.
body: VIA Foundation's Restoration Leaders programme has trained over 5,000 young people across six countries in nursery management, agroforestry, remote-sensing monitoring, and restoration project finance since it launched in 2022.

Graduates go on to found their own restoration enterprises, join partner organisations as field technicians, or become community trainers themselves — creating a multiplier effect well beyond the programme's direct reach.
The programme is now VIA Foundation's largest single source of new green jobs, and a growing share of the Foundation's own field staff and grantee leadership are programme alumni.

news.title: 2024 Annual Impact Report: A Decade of Restoration Finance in Africa
body: VIA Foundation's 2024 Annual Impact Report reviews a decade of restoration finance across the continent, covering 131+ funded projects and over $28M in deployed capital.

The report details methodology updates to the Foundation's monitoring framework, country-level breakdowns of hectares restored and jobs created, and lessons learned from projects that underperformed their targets.
The full report, including downloadable data tables, will be available on the Annual Reports page.

news.title: Financing the AFR100 Commitment: Opportunities and Pathways
body: This publication examines the financing gap standing between AFR100's pan-African restoration pledge and its 2030 targets, and sets out the blended finance pathways VIA Foundation believes can close it.
It draws on VIA Foundation's own portfolio data to model how catalytic capital, deployed early, can mobilise a multiple of private co-investment across different landscape types.
The publication is aimed at funders, development finance institutions, and policymakers evaluating where restoration capital can have the greatest leverage.

news.title: VIA Foundation Joins Global Coalition for Nature-Based Solutions at COP29
body: VIA Foundation has joined the Global Coalition for Nature-Based Solutions, a coalition of restoration financiers, NGOs, and governments committing to coordinated action ahead of COP29.
As part of the coalition, VIA Foundation will share its monitoring and verification methodology as an open reference framework for other restoration funders operating in Africa.

"Restoration finance works best when funders aren't duplicating measurement systems or competing for the same grantees," said VIA Foundation CEO Assumpta Uzamukunda. "This coalition is about pulling in the same direction."
